Each stage produces evidence for the next stage.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Stage</th> <th>Agent action</th> <th>Permission</th> <th>Human gate</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Prepare</strong></td> <td>Read configuration, host-key record, key label, token scope, and expiry</td> <td>Local read</td> <td>Approve setup record</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Inspect</strong></td> <td>Clone or fetch through Git over SSH and query REST metadata</td> <td>Repository read and API read</td> <td>None after setup</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Analyze</strong></td> <td>Read files, branches, pull requests, and build status through approved tools</td> <td>Read-only MCP tools</td> <td>None for bounded reads</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Prepare change</strong></td> <td>Produce a patch, branch plan, or pull request draft in a local workspace</td> <td>Local write only</td> <td>Review diff and target</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Approve write</strong></td> <td>Present exact remote action, scope, and rollback path</td> <td>No remote write yet</td> <td>Human approval</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execute write</strong></td> <td>Push a branch, create a pull request, or call a write endpoint</td> <td>Short-lived write identity</td> <td>Confirm each action</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Verify</strong></td> <td>Read the resulting commit, pull request, or status</td> <td>Read-only again</td> <td>Confirm expected result</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The default agent profile should stop after <strong>Analyze</strong> or <strong>Prepare change</strong>. A separate write profile should use a different token or key, a short expiry, a fixed target, and an approval prompt. A repository access key cannot perform the write step, which creates a useful technical boundary.</p> <h2 id="rollback-and-removal"> <a href="#rollback-and-removal" title="Rollback and Removal">Rollback and Removal</a> <a href="#rollback-and-removal" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Rollback and Removal">#</a> </h2> <p>Rollback starts with access removal, then local configuration cleanup:</p> <ol> <li>Remove the repository, project, or workspace access key from the matching Bitbucket settings page.</li> <li>Revoke the repository, project, workspace, or user API token in the matching Bitbucket security page.</li> <li>Remove the saved Teamwork Graph credential through the documented <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="authentication procedure"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/teamwork-graph/twg-cli/getting-started/how-authentication-works/"> <a href="https://developer.atlassian.com/platform/teamwork-graph/twg-cli/getting-started/how-authentication-works/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >authentication procedure</a> </span> for the installed CLI version. Preserve the prior credential only in the approved secret manager. Confirm the isolated profile no longer lists the test credential.</li> <li>Remove the repository <code>.gitconfig</code> file and its <code>includeIf</code> entry after the test ends. Keep unrelated Git configuration unchanged.</li> <li>Remove only the verified Bitbucket host-key line added for the test. Retain other approved host keys.</li> <li>Remove the external <code>agent.env</code> file and temporary output. Remove the MCP server entry from the host configuration, then restart the host.</li> </ol> <p>Record each removal, the operator, and the time. Rotate a key or token when a value entered an unexpected log, process record, or transcript.</p> <h2 id="a-remote-read-loop-with-local-reference-updates"> <a href="#a-remote-read-loop-with-local-reference-updates" title="A Remote-Read Loop With Local Reference Updates">A Remote-Read Loop With Local Reference Updates</a> <a href="#a-remote-read-loop-with-local-reference-updates" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="A Remote-Read Loop With Local Reference Updates">#</a> </h2> <p>Use a small loop for recurring repository inspection:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>LOCAL_REPO<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#e6db74">"<local-directory>"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git -C <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$LOCAL_REPO<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> fetch --no-tags </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git -C <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$LOCAL_REPO<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> status --short --branch </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git -C <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$LOCAL_REPO<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> log -1 --format<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#e6db74">'%H %ad %s'</span> --date<span style="color:#f92672">=</span>iso-strict </span></span></code></pre></div><p><code>HEAD</code> means the repository’s current checked-out reference. A successful result proves one permitted SSH identity reached the named repository. It does not prove which key was selected or whether push access exists.</p> <p><strong>Expected output:</strong> a fetch result, branch status, and one commit line. Untested example. <code>fetch</code> performs no remote write, but it updates local references and <code>FETCH_HEAD</code>. The loop does not push or change branches.</p> <p>The MCP server should expose the same read boundary through named operations. A local shell wrapper or MCP tool should reject a write verb before sending a request. Log the tool name, repository placeholder, revision, result class, and duration. Redact tokens, cookies, private paths, and file contents unless the task explicitly needs one file.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="permission-denied-publickey"> <a href="#permission-denied-publickey" title="Permission denied (publickey)"><code>Permission denied (publickey)</code></a> <a href="#permission-denied-publickey" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Permission denied (publickey)">#</a> </h3> <p>Check the active agent socket, the selected public key, the repository access-key entry, and <code>IdentitiesOnly</code>. A repository key needs to exist on the target repository or project. A personal key needs account permission. A workspace access key has a different write boundary.</p> <h3 id="the-wrong-repository-key-is-offered"> <a href="#the-wrong-repository-key-is-offered" title="The wrong repository key is offered">The wrong repository key is offered</a> <a href="#the-wrong-repository-key-is-offered" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The wrong repository key is offered">#</a> </h3> <p>Use one key per repository with <code>core.sshCommand</code>, or group clones under a directory controlled by <code>includeIf</code>. List agent keys with <code>ssh-add -l</code>. If many 1Password keys are available, use an explicit identity selector or a 1Password SSH bookmark. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="1Password Agent guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.1password.dev/ssh/agent"> <a href="https://www.1password.dev/ssh/agent" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >1Password Agent guide</a> </span> documents the key-count and bookmark considerations.</p> <h3 id="ssh-reports-a-changed-host-key"> <a href="#ssh-reports-a-changed-host-key" title="SSH reports a changed host key">SSH reports a changed host key</a> <a href="#ssh-reports-a-changed-host-key" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="SSH reports a changed host key">#</a> </h3> <p>Stop the agent. Do not delete <code>known_hosts</code> as a first response. Compare the current Bitbucket Cloud host-key record with the local entry through an independent channel. Remove or replace an entry only after the comparison passes.</p> <h3 id="the-api-returns-401-or-403"> <a href="#the-api-returns-401-or-403" title="The API returns 401 or 403">The API returns <code>401</code> or <code>403</code></a> <a href="#the-api-returns-401-or-403" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The API returns 401 or 403">#</a> </h3> <p>Check token expiry, token type, endpoint scope, and the account or workspace boundary. A repository read scope does not include pull requests. A write endpoint needs a write scope and an approved write profile. Do not widen scopes until the failed endpoint is named.</p> <h3 id="the-api-returns-repository-data-but-no-pull-requests"> <a href="#the-api-returns-repository-data-but-no-pull-requests" title="The API returns repository data but no pull requests">The API returns repository data but no pull requests</a> <a href="#the-api-returns-repository-data-but-no-pull-requests" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The API returns repository data but no pull requests">#</a> </h3> <p>Add the smallest pull request read scope in a new or rotated token. Do not reuse a broad user token for a read-only MCP server.</p> <h3 id="the-mcp-server-lists-tools-but-a-call-fails"> <a href="#the-mcp-server-lists-tools-but-a-call-fails" title="The MCP server lists tools but a call fails">The MCP server lists tools but a call fails</a> <a href="#the-mcp-server-lists-tools-but-a-call-fails" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The MCP server lists tools but a call fails">#</a> </h3> <p>Separate server registration, connection, tool discovery, execution, and result verification. Inspect the server log without exposing the token. Verify the endpoint and input shape. Retry once after checking connectivity. Mark the operation incomplete when the second call fails.</p> <h3 id="a-third-party-bitbucket-cli-asks-for-broad-access"> <a href="#a-third-party-bitbucket-cli-asks-for-broad-access" title="A third-party Bitbucket CLI asks for broad access">A third-party Bitbucket CLI asks for broad access</a> <a href="#a-third-party-bitbucket-cli-asks-for-broad-access" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="A third-party Bitbucket CLI asks for broad access">#</a> </h3> <p>Stop installation. Compare the requested access with the task record. Review source, release signatures or checksums, network destinations, secret storage, and write behavior. The official Atlassian CLI command reference does not establish support for a third-party Bitbucket binary.</p> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Create a short access record with the repository or project scope, key label, host-key verification date, API scopes, token expiry, 1Password owner, MCP tool allowlist, log policy, and write approver.</p> <p>Run one read-only clone, one REST metadata read, and one MCP tool read with placeholders in the transcript. Compare the results. Keep the agent profile read-only until the record and logs pass review.</p> <p>When a write task arrives, prepare a local diff first. Present the target branch, changed paths, requested API method, token scope, and rollback step. Use a separate short-lived write identity only after a human approves the exact action.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Detection and Incident Response Capstone Answer Key
item.description: Compare a completed detection and incident response package with the reference evidence, rule, recovery plan, and executive update.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the Detection Engineering and Incident Response Capstone"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/08-capstone/"> <a href="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/08-capstone/" rel="follow me" >Return to the Detection Engineering and Incident Response Capstone</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Open this reference after you finish and score your capstone.</strong> Record each difference as a correction, unsupported claim, or remaining evidence gap.</p> <h2 id="incident-decision"> <a href="#incident-decision" title="Incident Decision">Incident Decision</a> <a href="#incident-decision" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Incident Decision">#</a> </h2> <p>Declare a high-severity incident with high confidence in endpoint compromise and identity misuse. Treat the link between both paths as medium confidence until added provider or network evidence supports one actor or sequence.</p> <h2 id="evidence-record"> <a href="#evidence-record" title="Evidence Record">Evidence Record</a> <a href="#evidence-record" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Evidence Record">#</a> </h2> <p>These SHA-256 values cover the exact supplied files as published for this course. Recalculate them from your downloads before and after analysis. All times below are UTC. Identity-provider, mail-access, proxy, and script-content records are absent.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>File</th> <th style="text-align: right">Lines</th> <th>SHA-256</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><code>auth-events.jsonl</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">8</td> <td><code>fa4bbaf8693287f884d5592f5d401ed66fb0087daada87ed4db6454d0d6de5cb</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>endpoint-events.jsonl</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">8</td> <td><code>a3d053605d71798663ef947bb0f4424b0dfe2f0bbb6aa641c5820b5d5d9cdef1</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>dns-events.csv</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">7, including header</td> <td><code>14ddb700e39a3dd46d428d5c0dcda01550baf04e74028fba7744813d551615a9</code></td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="core-timeline"> <a href="#core-timeline" title="Core Timeline">Core Timeline</a> <a href="#core-timeline" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Core Timeline">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Time UTC</th> <th>ID</th> <th>Supported interpretation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>13:58:02</strong></td> <td>E-2001</td> <td>Outlook writes a macro-enabled document</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>13:59:28</strong></td> <td>E-2002</td> <td>Word opens the document</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:00:16</strong></td> <td>E-2003</td> <td>Word starts encoded PowerShell</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:00:24</strong></td> <td>D-3002</td> <td>The host resolves the suspicious test domain</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:00:31</strong></td> <td>E-2004</td> <td>PowerShell writes <code>sync-update.ps1</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:01:10</strong></td> <td>E-2005</td> <td>A scheduled task creates persistence</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:02:49</strong></td> <td>E-2006</td> <td>PowerShell connects to the DNS answer on TCP 443</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:04:09</strong></td> <td>A-1004</td> <td>Legacy-protocol sign-in succeeds after failures</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:06:41</strong></td> <td>A-1005</td> <td>A mailbox rule hides invoice mail</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>14:07:33</strong></td> <td>A-1006</td> <td>A mail-reading OAuth grant is approved</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The endpoint and identity chains overlap. Shared timing and identity support correlation, while the available sources do not prove a single actor or causal sequence.</p> <h2 id="scope"> <a href="#scope" title="Scope">Scope</a> <a href="#scope" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Scope">#</a> </h2> <p>As of <code>2026-06-18T15:00:00Z</code>, confirmed scope includes Morgan’s identity and <code>HR-LT-044</code>. Likely scope includes mail reachable through the delegated grant. Exclude <code>FIN-LT-021</code> after comparing its approved inventory chain. Unknowns include message access, script content, destination content, initial document delivery detail, and other activity tied to the indicators.</p> <h2 id="detection-package"> <a href="#detection-package" title="Detection Package">Detection Package</a> <a href="#detection-package" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Detection Package">#</a> </h2> <p>The strongest first rule detects Office starting encoded PowerShell. A second analytic should correlate the same host with a dropped script, scheduled task, DNS request, or outbound connection within a short window. Identity analytics should cover failed-to-successful legacy access, suspicious mailbox rule creation, and risky delegated consent.</p> <p>Use this Sigma-style rule as the submitted draft. Its <code>test</code> status means no production validation is claimed. The backend field mapping and actual match results still need a local translator or SIEM test.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">title</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">Office Process Starts Encoded PowerShell</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">id</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">908e82a9-4f44-4f20-8da1-9e8af49fdb81</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">status</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">test</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">description</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">Detects an Office process starting PowerShell with an encoded command.</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">logsource</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">category</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">process_creation</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">product</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">windows</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">detection</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">parent_office</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">ParentImage|endswith</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">'\WINWORD.EXE'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">'\EXCEL.EXE'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">'\POWERPNT.EXE'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">child_powershell</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">Image|endswith</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">'\powershell.exe'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">'\pwsh.exe'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">encoded_flag</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">CommandLine|contains</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">'-EncodedCommand'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#e6db74">'-enc '</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#f92672">condition</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">parent_office and child_powershell and encoded_flag</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">falsepositives</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> - <span style="color:#ae81ff">Approved document automation after environment review</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">level</span>: <span style="color:#ae81ff">high</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p>The strategy card names Office-to-PowerShell execution, process parent and command-line fields, a 60-second host/user correlation window, approved automation as an exclusion candidate, and persistence or outbound activity as escalation evidence. Map the PowerShell behavior to T1059.001 and the scheduled-task evidence separately to T1053.005. Neither mapping proves malicious intent.</p> <p>The encoded-flag rule has a deliberate blind spot. Alternate PowerShell syntax, transformed or concatenated commands, another script host, or encoded content without <code>-EncodedCommand</code> need separate analytics. Record those evasion cases and their test results before claiming broad PowerShell coverage.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Case</th> <th>Input shape</th> <th>Expected rule result</th> <th>Observed result</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Positive 1</td> <td>Word starts PowerShell with <code>-EncodedCommand</code></td> <td>Match</td> <td>Offline checker: match</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Positive 2</td> <td>Excel starts <code>pwsh.exe</code> with <code>-enc</code></td> <td>Match</td> <td>Offline checker: match</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Negative 1</td> <td>Software Center starts an approved PowerShell file</td> <td>No match</td> <td>Offline checker: no match</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Negative 2</td> <td>Word starts a PDF viewer</td> <td>No match</td> <td>Offline checker: no match</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Boundary</td> <td>Word starts PowerShell without an encoded flag</td> <td>No match, review separate analytic</td> <td>Offline checker: no match</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The supplied <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="offline checker"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/downloads/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/check_rule_cases.py"> <a href="/downloads/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/check_rule_cases.py" rel="follow me" >offline checker</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="five cases"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/downloads/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/rule-test-events.jsonl"> <a href="/downloads/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/rule-test-events.jsonl" rel="follow me" >five cases</a> </span> produced <code>5/5 passed</code>, exit code 0, and zero matches among the two negative cases. For full offline credit, run the checker yourself, attach its output, and map its three predicates to the Sigma selections. Mark the backend query <code>not run, no SIEM translator available</code>. For a SIEM-backed submission, also attach the translated query, field mapping, observed results, and false-positive count. The offline checker does not execute the YAML or prove production behavior.</p> <h2 id="response-priorities"> <a href="#response-priorities" title="Response Priorities">Response Priorities</a> <a href="#response-priorities" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Response Priorities">#</a> </h2> <p>Preserve evidence, isolate the endpoint, restrict the identity, revoke sessions and grants, remove the preserved mailbox rule, collect artifacts, recover credentials, rebuild from trusted media, pass recovery gates, and monitor recurrence.</p> <p>The incident commander collects volatile endpoint evidence before isolation when active harm is controlled. If active exfiltration continues, contain first and record the evidence tradeoff. Use these five action-card exemplars:</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Action and owner</th> <th>Evidence and approval before change</th> <th>Success check</th> <th>Rollback or recovery</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Isolate <code>HR-LT-044</code>, endpoint lead</td> <td>Incident commander approval, endpoint and volatile data decision</td> <td>Host loses unapproved network paths</td> <td>Restore approved connectivity after trusted rebuild</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Restrict Morgan’s identity, identity lead</td> <td>Export sign-in and session records, approve business interruption</td> <td>Old sessions fail and new access uses approved MFA</td> <td>Temporary scoped access through incident authority</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Revoke OAuth grant, identity lead</td> <td>Preserve consent and application IDs</td> <td>Grant absent and old token path fails</td> <td>Reauthorize a reviewed app if business owner confirms need</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Remove mailbox rule, mail lead</td> <td>Export rule definition and message trace</td> <td>Rule absent and new mail follows normal routing</td> <td>Restore only a verified business rule</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Rebuild endpoint, endpoint lead</td> <td>Preserve document, script, task, hashes, and chain of custody</td> <td>Trusted image boots, old task absent, detections healthy</td> <td>Keep device isolated and restore approved backup</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Each action card needs a timestamp and approval ID in the learner’s submitted package.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Recovery gate</th> <th>Evidence required before closure</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Identity</td> <td>Credential and factor recovery, session revocation, consent review</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Endpoint</td> <td>Trusted rebuild, patches, healthy agent, no old task or script</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Mail</td> <td>Rule review and message trace preserved</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Monitoring</td> <td>Behavior detections active with owner, expiry, and test result</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Business</td> <td>Service owner accepts restored function and residual risk</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Improvement item</th> <th>Owner</th> <th>Validation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Limit legacy authentication</td> <td>Identity engineering</td> <td>Test a blocked legacy sign-in and approved modern sign-in</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Alert on risky delegated consent</td> <td>Identity engineering</td> <td>Replay a synthetic consent event into the alert path</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Keep process parent and command line</td> <td>Endpoint engineering</td> <td>Verify both fields arrive from a managed test host</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Detect unsanctioned scheduled tasks</td> <td>Detection engineering</td> <td>Positive and approved-task negative replay</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Correlate DNS and endpoint connections</td> <td>Network engineering</td> <td>Resolve and connect in an isolated test, verify host join</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Tune Office-to-PowerShell rule</td> <td>SOC detection owner</td> <td>Run five-case matrix and record alert volume</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="executive-update"> <a href="#executive-update" title="Executive Update">Executive Update</a> <a href="#executive-update" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Executive Update">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Security declared an incident involving one employee identity and one managed </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Windows endpoint. Evidence shows suspicious cloud access, delegated mail access, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>document-driven script execution, persistence, and outbound communication. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Containment and evidence preservation are in progress. Mail access volume and </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>the script's full behavior remain under investigation, with the next update due </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>after identity and endpoint collection finishes. </span></span></code></pre></div><h2 id="review-gate"> <a href="#review-gate" title="Review Gate">Review Gate</a> <a href="#review-gate" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Review Gate">#</a> </h2> <p>Use the rubric on the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="capstone prompt"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/08-capstone/"> <a href="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/08-capstone/" rel="follow me" >capstone prompt</a> </span> . Pass with <strong>80 out of 100 or higher</strong> and no evidence-integrity failure.</p> <h2 id="verify-your-review"> <a href="#verify-your-review" title="Verify Your Review">Verify Your Review</a> <a href="#verify-your-review" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Your Review">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> Each correction points to evidence or a stated limitation</li> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> Unsupported attribution and impact claims are removed</li> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> The score reaches 80 out of 100</li> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> No evidence-integrity failure remains</li> </ul> <p>Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Detection Engineering and Incident Response Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course-start/"> <a href="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Detection Engineering and Incident Response Course</a> </span> after you record corrections and the final score.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Detection Engineering and Incident Response Quiz Answer Key
item.description: Score the Detection Engineering and Incident Response quiz, review each reason, and complete the required corrections before the capstone.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the Detection Engineering and Incident Response Quiz"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/07-quiz/"> <a href="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/07-quiz/" rel="follow me" >Return to the Detection Engineering and Incident Response Quiz</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Use this key after you answer every question.</strong> Correct the reason for each missed item before you retake the quiz or start the capstone.</p> <h2 id="answer-key"> <a href="#answer-key" title="Answer Key">Answer Key</a> <a href="#answer-key" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Answer Key">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>B.</strong> A telemetry contract defines meaning and limits before analysis.</li> <li><strong>A.</strong> An Analytic holds platform-specific detection logic under a Detection Strategy.</li> <li><strong>C.</strong> ATT&CK v18 introduced the current defensive object model and deprecated Data Sources.</li> <li><strong>C.</strong> Approved inventory work should not match the Office-parent encoded-command rule.</li> <li><strong>B.</strong> The source proves use of an authentication path, not the human behind the session.</li> <li><strong>B.</strong> The event directly records the host behavior.</li> <li><strong>A.</strong> The card makes authority, evidence risk, rollback, and verification visible.</li> <li><strong>B.</strong> Password reset alone does not remove sessions or delegated application grants.</li> <li><strong>B.</strong> Parent, script, destination, user, and approval context support a separate benign workflow.</li> <li><strong>C.</strong> Recovery needs technical and business validation.</li> </ol> <h2 id="score-and-review"> <a href="#score-and-review" title="Score and Review">Score and Review</a> <a href="#score-and-review" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Score and Review">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Score</th> <th>Required next action</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>9 to 10</strong></td> <td>Record corrections for missed items, then start the capstone</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>7 to 8</strong></td> <td>Revisit each missed lesson, correct every missed reason, and retake the quiz from a clean copy. Start the capstone only after the retest reaches 9 out of 10</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>0 to 6</strong></td> <td>Repeat Lessons 1 through 6 with the sample timeline, correct every missed reason, and retake the quiz. Reach 9 out of 10 before the capstone</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Two answers seem plausible:</strong> Choose the one supported by direct evidence and bounded claims.</li> <li><strong>A framework term is unclear:</strong> Return to the official source linked in the related lesson.</li> <li><strong>Your reason differs from the key:</strong> Identify which fact changes the decision.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verify-your-review"> <a href="#verify-your-review" title="Verify Your Review">Verify Your Review</a> <a href="#verify-your-review" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Your Review">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> All ten questions have recorded answers and reasons</li> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> Missed items link to a specific lesson</li> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> Revised answers explain the evidence change</li> <li><input disabled="" type="checkbox"> The final score reaches 9 out of 10 before capstone work</li> </ul> <p>Complete the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Detection Engineering and Incident Response Capstone"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/08-capstone/"> <a href="/detection-engineering-incident-response-course/08-capstone/" rel="follow me" >Detection Engineering and Incident Response Capstone</a> </span> after you pass the quiz gate.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Local AI Secure Server Capstone Answer Key
item.description: Compare a completed Local AI Secure Server capstone package with the beginner and advanced reference decisions.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the capstone"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course/07-capstone/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course/07-capstone/" rel="follow me" >Return to the capstone</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Use this reference after completing your package and deployment decision.</strong> Compare its scope, evidence, conditions, and open risks with your own record.</p> <h2 id="beginner-reference"> <a href="#beginner-reference" title="Beginner Reference">Beginner Reference</a> <a href="#beginner-reference" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Beginner Reference">#</a> </h2> <p>A strong beginner decision reads:</p> <blockquote> <p>Approve for one local user with synthetic and low-sensitivity data. The runtime listens on loopback. The selected model fits with measured memory headroom. Three warm trials meet the stated response target. Remote access is absent. The prior configuration and model record support rollback.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="advanced-reference"> <a href="#advanced-reference" title="Advanced Reference">Advanced Reference</a> <a href="#advanced-reference" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Advanced Reference">#</a> </h2> <p>A strong advanced decision reads:</p> <blockquote> <p>Approve for approved private-network users after observed timeout and concurrency overload tests pass. The native runtime stays on loopback. An authenticated TLS gateway enforces per-user model access, request size, output, rate, and concurrency limits. Access tests show unauthorized and oversized requests denied before inference. Protected logs retain metadata under the stated schedule. Production data waits for privacy, legal, and incident reviews.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="reconcile-your-decision"> <a href="#reconcile-your-decision" title="Reconcile Your Decision">Reconcile Your Decision</a> <a href="#reconcile-your-decision" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Reconcile Your Decision">#</a> </h2> <p>For each difference, record your original claim, the evidence in your package, the corrected claim, and any change to the decision. Keep synthetic gateway results separate from tests against your own server.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Beginner gate:</strong> Confirm all nine files, model identity and license evidence, three warm trials, loopback binding, firewall policy, rollback results, and owners for remaining conditions.</li> <li><strong>Beginner rollback reference:</strong> Preserve a pre-change configuration file and hash, apply one controlled lab-only change, record health, listener, and denial results, restore the saved file, repeat those checks, and record cleanup. A narrative without before and after evidence does not pass the rollback gate.</li> <li><strong>Advanced gate:</strong> Confirm all nine files, artifact digest and retention, evaluation and capacity records, private gateway design, identity and logging controls, unauthorized and oversized denial tests, observed timeout and concurrency overload results, rollback results, and owners for remaining conditions. A missing timeout or overload result blocks approval.</li> </ul> <p>Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course-start/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course-start/" rel="follow me" >course hub</a> </span> after your package meets the selected track gate.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Local AI Secure Server Knowledge Check Answer Key
item.description: Score the Local AI Secure Server knowledge check, repair missed concepts, and verify the security gate before the capstone.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the knowledge check"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course/06-knowledge-check/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course/06-knowledge-check/" rel="follow me" >Return to the knowledge check</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Open this key after answering all ten questions.</strong> Compare each choice and reason with the table. Record every correction in <strong><code>local-ai-knowledge-check.md</code></strong>.</p> <h2 id="answer-key"> <a href="#answer-key" title="Answer Key">Answer Key</a> <a href="#answer-key" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Answer Key">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>#</th> <th>Answer</th> <th>Reason</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>1</strong></td> <td>B</td> <td>Weights form one part of runtime memory use.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>2</strong></td> <td>C</td> <td>A digest supports artifact identity against a known reference.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>3</strong></td> <td>A</td> <td>Prompt evaluation and generation measure different phases.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>4</strong></td> <td>B</td> <td>Loopback keeps early service access on one host.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>5</strong></td> <td>B</td> <td>Observed diagnostics and device activity establish placement.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>6</strong></td> <td>C</td> <td>The gateway supplies identity and policy while the runtime stays off the network.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>7</strong></td> <td>A</td> <td>Parallel requests multiply active context and raise memory demand.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>8</strong></td> <td>B</td> <td>Metadata supports operations while reducing raw-content collection.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>9</strong></td> <td>C</td> <td>Rollback needs the prior artifacts, settings, and evidence.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>10</strong></td> <td>B</td> <td>Unexpected broad binding requires containment and verification.</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="repair-missed-answers"> <a href="#repair-missed-answers" title="Repair Missed Answers">Repair Missed Answers</a> <a href="#repair-missed-answers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Repair Missed Answers">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Memory answers stay unclear:</strong> Revisit <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Lesson 1"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course/01-hardware-model-fit/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course/01-hardware-model-fit/" rel="follow me" >Lesson 1</a> </span> and your fit worksheet.</li> <li><strong>Performance terms blend together:</strong> Revisit <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Lesson 3"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course/03-measure-tune/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course/03-measure-tune/" rel="follow me" >Lesson 3</a> </span> and label both phases in your table.</li> <li><strong>Network controls seem redundant:</strong> Map the native runtime and gateway as separate processes with separate duties.</li> <li><strong>Rollback lacks a model artifact:</strong> Add the prior digest and storage location to your update record.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verify-completion"> <a href="#verify-completion" title="Verify Completion">Verify Completion</a> <a href="#verify-completion" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Completion">#</a> </h2> <p>Record your closed-book score and your score for questions 4, 6, 8, 9, and 10. Pass when the total reaches 8 out of 10, all five security questions are correct, and every miss links to a repaired lesson artifact.</p> <p>Continue with the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Local AI Server Capstone"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course/07-capstone/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course/07-capstone/" rel="follow me" >Local AI Server Capstone</a> </span> after you meet both gates.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Migrate a Hyper-V VM to Proxmox VE: A Reversible Checklist
item.description: Move one Hyper-V virtual machine to Proxmox VE with a stopped-source export, matched firmware, disk import, isolated boot test, and rollback plan.
item.content:encoded: <p>A <strong>Hyper-V export</strong> preserves a virtual machine’s files, while Proxmox VE needs a new guest configuration and imported VHDX virtual disk files. A successful copy alone does not prove the guest will boot or serve users. This checklist moves one VM through a stopped-source export, a controlled boot test, and a cutover with a clear return path.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Record the source:</strong> Capture firmware generation, disk paths, checkpoints, network settings, and encryption before export.</li> <li><strong>Stop writes:</strong> Shut down the Hyper-V VM before the final export and keep it off during the Proxmox test.</li> <li><strong>Match the boot path:</strong> Hyper-V Generation 1 uses legacy BIOS. Generation 2 uses UEFI.</li> <li><strong>Validate the service:</strong> Check data, network access, backups, and guest health before retiring the source.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>Plan a maintenance window and a test on a disposable VM first. You need administrator access to Hyper-V, Proxmox VE, storage for the export, and a verified backup separate from the migration copy. Allow time to transfer every virtual disk and test the guest application. Disk size and transfer speed set the downtime.</p> <p>This procedure covers a conventional VM with virtual disks. <strong>Shielded VMs, pass-through disks, shared disks, clustered workloads, and hardware-bound licensing</strong> need workload-specific plans. Record who owns the cutover decision and the latest time you will roll back. Do not start both copies on the production network with the same machine identity.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Source detail</th> <th>Why you need it</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>VM generation and firmware</strong></td> <td>Select SeaBIOS or OVMF on Proxmox</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Secure Boot state and template</strong></td> <td>Match the boot policy and enroll compatible keys</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Boot and data disks</strong></td> <td>Import every required VHDX virtual disk file in the right order</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Checkpoints and AVHDX files</strong></td> <td>Avoid treating a differencing disk as an independent base disk</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>IP, DNS, MAC, and VLAN</strong></td> <td>Restore reachability without creating a duplicate identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>vTPM and BitLocker</strong></td> <td>Prepare recovery before virtual hardware changes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Services and data checks</strong></td> <td>Define evidence for success and rollback</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Generation 1 uses legacy BIOS. Generation 2 uses Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI). An <strong>AVHDX file</strong> is a Hyper-V differencing disk linked to a base VHDX. A <strong>vTPM</strong> is a virtual Trusted Platform Module used by BitLocker and other security features. A <strong>VLAN</strong> is a separate logical network carried over shared network hardware.</p> <p><strong>SeaBIOS</strong> provides legacy BIOS firmware. <strong>OVMF</strong> provides UEFI firmware. <strong>VirtIO</strong> is a fast virtual device interface that needs guest drivers. An <strong>initramfs</strong> is the early Linux startup file system that loads drivers before the main system starts.</p> <h2 id="inventory-the-hyper-v-vm"> <a href="#inventory-the-hyper-v-vm" title="Inventory the Hyper-V VM">Inventory the Hyper-V VM</a> <a href="#inventory-the-hyper-v-vm" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inventory the Hyper-V VM">#</a> </h2> <p>Run these read-only commands in an elevated PowerShell session on the Hyper-V host. These are untested examples. Confirm each command against the installed Hyper-V module and your change procedure before use. Enter the VM name when prompted:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$vmName = Read-Host <span style="color:#e6db74">"Hyper-V VM name"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-VM -Name $vmName | Select-Object Name, State, Generation, ProcessorCount, MemoryAssigned </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName $vmName | Select-Object ControllerType, ControllerNumber, ControllerLocation, Path </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-VMSnapshot -VMName $vmName | Select-Object Name, CreationTime </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName $vmName | Select-Object Name, SwitchName, MacAddress </span></span></code></pre></div><p>The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Hyper-V PowerShell module"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Hyper-V PowerShell module</a> </span> documents these inventory commands. Compare disk paths with the VM settings and list any attached ISO, data disk, virtual switch, static address, or DHCP reservation. Record the guest OS and application versions. Verify the backup by restoring a test copy or checking a recent documented restore result. A file copy without a recovery test is weaker evidence.</p> <p>For a <strong>Generation 2</strong> VM, record its firmware and security settings as well:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-VMFirmware -VMName $vmName | Format-List * </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-VMSecurity -VMName $vmName | Format-List * </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Record the <strong>Secure Boot</strong> state, template, and vTPM setting. Microsoft’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Get-VMFirmware reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/get-vmfirmware"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/get-vmfirmware" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><strong><code>Get-VMFirmware</code></strong> reference</a> </span> limits the command to Generation 2. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Get-VMSecurity"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/get-vmsecurity"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/get-vmsecurity" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><strong><code>Get-VMSecurity</code></strong></a> </span> reports the VM security configuration. Do not run <strong><code>Get-VMFirmware</code></strong> against a Generation 1 guest. A <strong>MAC address</strong> identifies a network interface. <strong>DNS</strong> maps names to addresses. <strong>DHCP</strong> assigns network settings. An <strong>EFI disk</strong> stores UEFI settings.</p> <p><strong>Resolve checkpoints before the final export.</strong> Microsoft says a Hyper-V export gathers checkpoint files as well as VHDX disks. Deleting a checkpoint through Hyper-V merges its differencing disk. Never delete an <strong><code>.avhdx</code></strong> file in the filesystem to clear a checkpoint. If a merge fails or a disk chain looks incomplete, stop and follow <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s checkpoint recovery guidance"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v-snapshots-checkpoints-differencing-disks"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v-snapshots-checkpoints-differencing-disks" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s checkpoint recovery guidance</a> </span> . <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s checkpoint guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/checkpoints"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/checkpoints" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s checkpoint guide</a> </span> explains normal deletion and merging.</p> <p>For a Windows guest using <strong>BitLocker</strong> or a <strong>virtual TPM</strong>, obtain and verify the recovery key before changing virtual hardware. Hyper-V’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Generation 2 security documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/generation-2-virtual-machine-security-features"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/generation-2-virtual-machine-security-features" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Generation 2 security documentation</a> </span> describes vTPM-backed encryption. Microsoft’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="BitLocker FAQ"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/information-protection/bitlocker/bitlocker-key-management-faq"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/information-protection/bitlocker/bitlocker-key-management-faq" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >BitLocker FAQ</a> </span> explains why boot changes trigger recovery. A new Proxmox TPM device does not reproduce the old TPM state. Keep the key outside the exported VM.</p> <h2 id="export-a-stopped-vm"> <a href="#export-a-stopped-vm" title="Export a Stopped VM">Export a Stopped VM</a> <a href="#export-a-stopped-vm" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Export a Stopped VM">#</a> </h2> <p>Shut down the guest cleanly. Confirm Hyper-V shows <strong>Off</strong>, not Saved. Wait for any checkpoint merge to finish, then export the VM to a location with enough free space. In Hyper-V Manager, right-click the VM, choose <strong>Export</strong>, and select the destination. The PowerShell equivalent is:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$vmName = Read-Host <span style="color:#e6db74">"Stopped Hyper-V VM name"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$exportPath = Read-Host <span style="color:#e6db74">"Export destination directory"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>$vm = Get-VM -Name $vmName -ErrorAction Stop </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> ($vm.State <span style="color:#f92672">-ne</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'Off'</span>) { <span style="color:#66d9ef">throw</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"Stop the VM and wait for Hyper-V to show Off before exporting."</span> } </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Export-VM -Name $vmName -Path $exportPath </span></span></code></pre></div><p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s export guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/deploy/export-and-import-virtual-machines"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/deploy/export-and-import-virtual-machines" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s export guide</a> </span> says an export contains virtual disks, configuration, and checkpoint files. Its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Export-VM reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/export-vm"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/export-vm" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><strong><code>Export-VM</code></strong> reference</a> </span> defines the command. Confirm the expected disk files and sizes at the destination. Retain the stopped source VM and its independent backup. <strong>Do not modify the exported files while importing them.</strong></p> <p>Transfer the VHDX files to a path accessible from the Proxmox host. Treat the export as sensitive guest data. Use encrypted transport, restrict access to the transfer location and target storage, and remove temporary copies after validation. Check available capacity on both the transfer location and target storage. Preserve an untouched export for rollback. If the export contains <strong><code>.avhdx</code></strong> files, do not pick a base <strong><code>.vhdx</code></strong> by filename and assume it contains the latest writes. Resolve the disk chain on Hyper-V before continuing.</p> <h2 id="create-the-proxmox-shell"> <a href="#create-the-proxmox-shell" title="Create the Proxmox Shell">Create the Proxmox Shell</a> <a href="#create-the-proxmox-shell" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create the Proxmox Shell">#</a> </h2> <p>Create a new VM in the Proxmox web interface with the guest OS type, CPU, and memory recorded earlier. Choose a new unused VM ID. Do not install a fresh operating system. Remove the empty disk created by the wizard before you import the source disk. Leave the network adapter disconnected from the production bridge for the first boot, or attach it to an isolated test network.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Hyper-V source</th> <th>Proxmox target</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Generation 1, legacy BIOS</strong></td> <td>SeaBIOS</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Generation 2, UEFI</strong></td> <td>OVMF with an EFI disk and matching Secure Boot policy</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Windows boot disk without VirtIO storage driver</strong></td> <td>Attach initially as SATA</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Windows with vTPM or BitLocker</strong></td> <td>New TPM state device when needed, recovery key ready before first boot</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Microsoft’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="VM generation guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/plan/Should-I-create-a-generation-1-or-2-virtual-machine-in-Hyper-V"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/virtualization/hyper-v/plan/Should-I-create-a-generation-1-or-2-virtual-machine-in-Hyper-V" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >VM generation guide</a> </span> maps Generation 1 to legacy BIOS and Generation 2 to UEFI. Proxmox’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="VM documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >VM documentation</a> </span> documents SeaBIOS, OVMF, and the EFI disk used to keep UEFI settings. <strong>Match the source boot mode.</strong> Changing it during migration creates another boot problem to diagnose.</p> <p>For a Generation 2 source, match whether <strong>Secure Boot</strong> was enabled. Check the source template and select compatible enrolled keys for the guest. Hyper-V template names do not transfer to Proxmox. Proxmox’s 4 MB EFI disk and <strong>Pre-Enroll keys</strong> option supply Secure Boot keys and enable Secure Boot by default. Verify the target’s boot behavior before cutover. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Microsoft’s firmware reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/set-vmfirmware"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/hyper-v/set-vmfirmware" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Microsoft’s firmware reference</a> </span> describes the source template requirement. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox’s EFI disk documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Proxmox’s EFI disk documentation</a> </span> describes the target keys.</p> <p>Before changing EFI keys, verify the recovery key is escrowed and record the current protector IDs. Follow the installed Proxmox VE and OVMF documentation for EFI-key enrollment. Reconfirm the recovery key and verify <code>manage-bde -status</code> before first boot. Do not suspend, disable, or delete protectors as a generic migration step. Record the firmware package version, Secure Boot state and firmware version, and BitLocker state.</p> <p>If the source uses a <strong>vTPM</strong>, add <strong>TPM State</strong> in Proxmox’s Hardware panel before the first boot. Select <strong>version 2.0</strong> unless the source guest has a documented requirement for version 1.2. This creates new TPM state, not a copy of the Hyper-V vTPM. A BitLocker guest needs its verified recovery key at first boot. Proxmox’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="TPM documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >TPM documentation</a> </span> describes the Hardware action and versions.</p> <p>For Windows, start with a SATA boot disk unless the guest already has the required VirtIO storage driver. After a successful boot, install the supported VirtIO drivers and change one virtual device at a time. Proxmox recommends VirtIO SCSI for performance, but a missing boot driver leaves Windows unable to access its system disk. For Linux, check whether the initramfs includes the target storage driver before switching buses. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox VM documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Proxmox VM documentation</a> </span> describes the disk controllers.</p> <h2 id="import-and-attach-disks"> <a href="#import-and-attach-disks" title="Import and Attach Disks">Import and Attach Disks</a> <a href="#import-and-attach-disks" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Import and Attach Disks">#</a> </h2> <p>On the Proxmox host, check the copied VHDX path. The following command illustrates an import for VM ID <strong>230</strong> into a storage ID named <strong><code>local-lvm</code></strong>. Replace all three values with your own:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>qm disk import <span style="color:#ae81ff">230</span> /path/to/exported/boot.vhdx local-lvm </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Proxmox’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="qm disk import reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/generated/qm.1-synopsis.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/generated/qm.1-synopsis.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><strong><code>qm disk import</code></strong> reference</a> </span> says the source image is imported as an <strong>unused disk</strong>. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="QEMU’s image documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/system/images"> <a href="https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/system/images" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >QEMU’s image documentation</a> </span> lists VHDX as a supported conversion format. Import each additional data disk separately. Wait for each import task to finish and compare the imported disk sizes with the source inventory.</p> <p>In the VM’s <strong>Hardware</strong> panel, attach the unused boot disk as <strong>SATA</strong> for the first Windows boot. Attach data disks in a documented order. In <strong>Options > Boot Order</strong>, select the boot disk. For a Generation 2 guest, verify <strong>OVMF</strong> and the EFI disk. Keep the import files and source VM intact until validation passes.</p> <h2 id="test-before-cutover"> <a href="#test-before-cutover" title="Test Before Cutover">Test Before Cutover</a> <a href="#test-before-cutover" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Test Before Cutover">#</a> </h2> <p>Start the Proxmox guest on the isolated network. Use the console to check the boot screen, operating system login, disk volumes, application data, and service logs. A login prompt alone does not prove migration success. Use the checks you recorded before export, including a representative transaction or read of recent data.</p> <p>For a BitLocker guest, unlock with the recovery key if prompted. After Windows starts, check the operating system volume’s protection status and protectors from an elevated prompt:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>manage-bde -status C: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>manage-bde -protectors -get C: </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Microsoft’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="BitLocker operations guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/operations-guide"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/data-protection/bitlocker/operations-guide" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >BitLocker operations guide</a> </span> documents protector inspection and recovery-key backup. The output includes sensitive recovery material. Do not paste it into a ticket or public log. Verify the intended protector and escrow a current recovery method under your policy. Restart the guest and confirm it boots without another recovery prompt before cutover. Repeated recovery is a failed migration check, not a prompt to discard the original key.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Test</th> <th>Pass condition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Boot and disks</strong></td> <td>Guest starts and every expected volume mounts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Secure Boot and BitLocker</strong></td> <td>Intended boot policy holds and encrypted guest restarts without repeated recovery</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Application</strong></td> <td>A representative read or transaction succeeds</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Network</strong></td> <td>Required peers reach the test guest on intended ports</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Proxmox backup and isolated restore test succeed before source retirement</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Operations</strong></td> <td>Monitoring, time sync, shutdown, and guest agent behave as intended</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>When the application checks pass, switch its production network path or address during the maintenance window. Keep Hyper-V powered off. A changed virtual NIC might require a new DHCP reservation or a corrected static address inside the guest. Check DNS, firewall rules, and dependent services from a separate client. Proxmox’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="VM documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >VM documentation</a> </span> covers network device and guest-agent options.</p> <h2 id="troubleshoot-and-roll-back"> <a href="#troubleshoot-and-roll-back" title="Troubleshoot and Roll Back">Troubleshoot and Roll Back</a> <a href="#troubleshoot-and-roll-back" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshoot and Roll Back">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Symptom</th> <th>First check</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>No boot device</strong></td> <td>Boot order, imported boot disk, BIOS versus UEFI mode, and Secure Boot keys</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Windows storage error</strong></td> <td>SATA attachment and missing VirtIO storage driver</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Repeated BitLocker recovery prompt</strong></td> <td>New TPM state, Secure Boot policy, boot measurements, and protectors</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Guest boots without network</strong></td> <td>New virtual NIC, bridge, VLAN, DHCP reservation, and static address</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Data is old or missing</strong></td> <td>Wrong VHDX, incomplete export, checkpoint chain, or missing data disk</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>If a required test fails before the rollback deadline, stop the Proxmox VM and disconnect its production network. Restore the source network path, then start the original Hyper-V VM. <strong>Never run both copies with the same production identity.</strong> Record any writes accepted by the Proxmox copy before returning to Hyper-V. Those writes need separate recovery or reconciliation because the source disk did not receive them.</p> <p>Keep the source VM and export until the Proxmox guest has passed your service checks, a new backup, an isolated restore test, and an agreed observation period. The site’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="virtualization comparison"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/vmware-esxi-citrix-xenserver-hyper-v-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/vmware-esxi-citrix-xenserver-hyper-v-comparison/" rel="follow me" >virtualization comparison</a> </span> helps with platform choice. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox upgrade guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/proxmox-ve-8-to-9-upgrade-guide/"> <a href="/articles/proxmox-ve-8-to-9-upgrade-guide/" rel="follow me" >Proxmox upgrade guide</a> </span> covers a later maintenance task. <strong>A migration ends after the workload and recovery path work on the new host, not when the disk import completes.</strong></p> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Keep the source VM and export until workload checks, backup checks, and rollback checks pass during the agreed observation period. Review the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox VM backup restore drill"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/proxmox-vm-backup-restore-drill/"> <a href="/articles/proxmox-vm-backup-restore-drill/" rel="follow me" >Proxmox VM backup restore drill</a> </span> before retiring the source.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Proxmox VM Backup Restore Drill: Prove the Guest Works
item.description: Test a Proxmox VM backup with an isolated restore. Check disk coverage, backup mode, guest data, service health, and recovery time without touching production.
item.content:encoded: <p>A green backup task tells you Proxmox wrote a backup. The task does not show whether the guest boots, its data is recent, or its main service works. <strong>Restore a copy under a new VM ID on an isolated network.</strong> The result gives you evidence for recovery before an outage forces the test.</p> <p>This drill covers one <strong>Proxmox VE virtual machine</strong>. Containers have different backup rules, especially for bind and device mounts. The site’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="homelab backup restore drill"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/homelab-backup-restore-drill/"> <a href="/articles/homelab-backup-restore-drill/" rel="follow me" >homelab backup restore drill</a> </span> covers broader file recovery. Here, you will test a Proxmox VM backup and its workload.</p> <p>A <strong>guest</strong> is the operating system running inside a virtual machine. <strong>Bind mounts</strong> and <strong>device mounts</strong> expose host resources to a guest. Test those resources through a separate recovery plan.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Define success first:</strong> Name a data item, a service check, and an acceptable recovery time.</li> <li><strong>Inspect coverage:</strong> A VM backup skips disks marked <strong>No backup</strong> and cannot recreate external services or omitted data.</li> <li><strong>Restore separately:</strong> Use an unused VM ID and keep the restored network isolated from production.</li> <li><strong>Record evidence:</strong> Measure backup age, restore time, boot, disk presence, and a real application check.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>Choose a VM whose backup is safe to test. You need Proxmox administrator access, a completed backup on file storage or Proxmox Backup Server (PBS), enough space for a second VM, and an isolated bridge or disconnected network device. An isolated bridge is a Proxmox virtual network with no route to your production LAN. Use a disconnected adapter or a test VLAN when you do not have one. Keep the production VM running. Reserve a new VM ID, such as <strong>920</strong>, after checking whether another guest uses the ID. Plan enough time for a full restore and a workload test.</p> <p>Write the pass condition before restoring. For a file server, pick a recent file and its expected checksum or contents. For a database, pick a safe read query and a record written before the backup. For a web service, pick a local health check and a representative page. Record the latest acceptable data timestamp, your <strong>recovery point objective (RPO)</strong>, and the time allowed to restore service, your <strong>recovery time objective (RTO)</strong>. A boot screen alone does not meet these checks.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Record</th> <th>Example evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Backup point</strong></td> <td>Snapshot time and the last expected data item</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery target</strong></td> <td>Unused VM ID, target storage, isolated bridge</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Workload test</strong></td> <td>Login, volume mount, and application read</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Time limit</strong></td> <td>Start and finish time of the restore and service check</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Do not attach the restored guest to the production network before reviewing its name, IP address, MAC address, scheduled jobs, and external integrations. A copied identity might conflict with the running VM or send duplicate work.</p> <h2 id="inspect-what-the-backup-covers"> <a href="#inspect-what-the-backup-covers" title="Inspect What the Backup Covers">Inspect What the Backup Covers</a> <a href="#inspect-what-the-backup-covers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inspect What the Backup Covers">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Version scope:</strong> These examples were not executed during article preparation. Record the output of <code>pveversion --verbose</code> before testing. Use documentation matching the installed Proxmox VE release. Record the storage backend, guest type, and command output in the drill record.</p> <p>On a Proxmox node, the following read-only command shows the source VM configuration. Replace <strong>120</strong> with your source VM ID:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>qm config <span style="color:#ae81ff">120</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p>List every virtual disk and its backup setting. Proxmox’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="VM disk documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/qm.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >VM disk documentation</a> </span> says the <strong>No backup</strong> option excludes a disk from VM backup. Check whether application data sits on an excluded disk, a host mount, passed-through hardware, or a remote service. Record its separate recovery procedure. A VM boot test does not prove excluded data is protected.</p> <p>Check the latest backup’s timestamp, size, task log, and storage location. In the Proxmox interface, open the backup storage’s <strong>Backups</strong> view or the VM’s <strong>Backup</strong> tab. Confirm the job ended without errors. Proxmox’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="backup documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/vzdump.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/vzdump.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >backup documentation</a> </span> distinguishes regular backup files from PBS storage, which keeps deduplicated chunks and metadata.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backup mode</th> <th>VM behavior</th> <th>Decision for this drill</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Snapshot</strong></td> <td>Backs up a running VM with low downtime. Guest writes introduce a small consistency risk.</td> <td>Suitable for routine tests when the workload tolerates this recovery point.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Stop</strong></td> <td>Shuts down the guest for the backup start and gives the strongest consistency.</td> <td>Use when the workload requires a clean shutdown and the downtime is acceptable.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Suspend</strong></td> <td>Suspends before snapshot mode and adds downtime without a general consistency benefit.</td> <td>Avoid selecting suspend as a default improvement over snapshot.</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>These mode tradeoffs come from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox’s backup mode reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/vzdump.adoc"> <a href="https://github.com/proxmox/pve-docs/blob/master/vzdump.adoc" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Proxmox’s backup mode reference</a> </span> . A <strong>QEMU guest agent</strong> is a service inside the guest that lets Proxmox request actions such as filesystem freeze and thaw. A running guest with its guest agent enabled and healthy supports those actions during snapshot backup. Filesystem freeze improves consistency but does not replace a database-specific recovery check. Record the actual mode and guest-agent state instead of assuming a scheduled job uses your preferred settings.</p> <h2 id="create-or-select-a-recovery-point"> <a href="#create-or-select-a-recovery-point" title="Create or Select a Recovery Point">Create or Select a Recovery Point</a> <a href="#create-or-select-a-recovery-point" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Create or Select a Recovery Point">#</a> </h2> <p>Use a recent successful scheduled backup if the drill tests routine recovery. If you need a fresh one-time backup, select the VM’s <strong>Backup</strong> tab, choose <strong>Backup now</strong>, set the target storage and mode, and wait for the task log to report success. From a Proxmox shell, this example backs up VM <strong>120</strong> to a storage ID named <strong>backup-nfs</strong> in snapshot mode:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>vzdump <span style="color:#ae81ff">120</span> --storage backup-nfs --mode snapshot </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Replace both IDs with your own. Run the command only after confirming the storage accepts backups and has room for the job.
