style="text-align: right">2325.4</td> <td style="text-align: right">1938.5</td> <td style="text-align: right">1817.6</td> <td style="text-align: right">535.1</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>At 256K, the dual-card system led on GPT-OSS and Qwen3.5 prompt processing. The GB10 led on Nemotron, Qwen3.6, and Qwen3.8. Model architecture and runtime behavior matter as much as the memory interface.</p> <h2 id="supplemental-qwen38-flash-next-benchmarks"> <a href="#supplemental-qwen38-flash-next-benchmarks" title="Supplemental Qwen3.8 Flash-Next benchmarks">Supplemental Qwen3.8 Flash-Next benchmarks</a> <a href="#supplemental-qwen38-flash-next-benchmarks" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Supplemental Qwen3.8 Flash-Next benchmarks">#</a> </h2> <p>Three extra runs measured Qwen3.8 Flash-Next GGUF packages on the dual RTX 5060 Ti system at 4K and 16K context settings. The exact Hugging Face model reference and quantization appear in each row.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Exact model</th> <th style="text-align: right">Quantization</th> <th style="text-align: right">4K generation</th> <th style="text-align: right">16K generation</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="hf.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ2_XS"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/tree/main/IQ2_XS"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/tree/main/IQ2_XS" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><code>hf.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ2_XS</code></a> </span> </td> <td style="text-align: right">IQ2_XS</td> <td style="text-align: right">31.77 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">28.20 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="hf.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ3_S"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/tree/main/IQ3_S"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF/tree/main/IQ3_S" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><code>hf.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ3_S</code></a> </span> </td> <td style="text-align: right">IQ3_S</td> <td style="text-align: right">24.54 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">22.60 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="hf.co/orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-GGUF/tree/main"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-GGUF/tree/main" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><code>hf.co/orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M</code></a> </span> </td> <td style="text-align: right">Q4_K_M</td> <td style="text-align: right">17.91 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">17.02 tok/s</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The IQ2_XS package produced the highest throughput in this set. Its 4K result was 31.77 tokens per second, compared with 24.54 for IQ3_S and 17.91 for Q4_K_M. At 16K, the same order held at 28.20, 22.60, and 17.02 tokens per second.</p> <p>Run the same exact model references with Ollama:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama run hf.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ2_XS </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama run hf.co/ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF:IQ3_S </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama run hf.co/orcarouter/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Uncensored-GGUF:Q4_K_M </span></span></code></pre></div><p>These earlier supplemental rows are dual-GPU observations. They are separate from the matched RTX 5060 Ti versus GB10 request matrix above. The record omits resolved manifest digests, processed prompt-token counts, output length, warm state, device split, CPU, system RAM, cooling setup, and measurement date.</p> <h2 id="strata-versus-dense-ollama-at-256k"> <a href="#strata-versus-dense-ollama-at-256k" title="Strata versus dense Ollama at 256K">Strata versus dense Ollama at 256K</a> <a href="#strata-versus-dense-ollama-at-256k" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Strata versus dense Ollama at 256K">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A second benchmark from October 14, 2026 compared two model and runtime stacks on the same dual RTX 5060 Ti host.</strong> The dense baseline used <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="qwen3.8:27b"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://ollama.com/library/qwen3.8:27b"> <a href="https://ollama.com/library/qwen3.8:27b" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" ><code>qwen3.8:27b</code></a> </span> , a 27.3-billion-parameter Qwen35 model in Q4_K_M. Model architecture, quantization, packaging, expert routing, and inference engine changed together. The IQ3_S and Q4_K_M Flash variants were outside this pass.</p> <h3 id="test-system-and-method"> <a href="#test-system-and-method" title="Test system and method">Test system and method</a> <a href="#test-system-and-method" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Test system and method">#</a> </h3> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Component</th> <th>Recorded configuration</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>GPUs</strong></td> <td>2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, 16 GiB each, compute capability 12.0</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>GPU link</strong></td> <td>PCIe 4.0 x4 per card, PHB topology, no NVLink</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>CPU</strong></td> <td>AMD Ryzen 9 5900XT, 32 threads</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Host memory</strong></td> <td>62 GiB RAM and 15 GiB swap</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>NVIDIA driver</strong></td> <td>595.99.02</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The harness generated synthetic numbered records. Each row followed the format <code>Record 00001: alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta iota kappa.</code> The instruction required <code>BENCHMARK_OK</code> first, followed by a concise technical synthesis through the output limit. The six prompts contained 180, 720, 1,500, 3,100, 6,200, and 12,400 records.</p> <p>Each run used temperature 0, seed 42, and a maximum output length of 128 tokens. Treat the generation result as specific to these decode modes.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th style="text-align: right">Context setting</th> <th style="text-align: right">Dense prompt tokens</th> <th style="text-align: right">Flash prompt tokens</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>4K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">3,824</td> <td style="text-align: right">3,826</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>16K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">15,164</td> <td style="text-align: right">15,166</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>32K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">31,544</td> <td style="text-align: right">31,546</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>64K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">65,144</td> <td style="text-align: right">65,146</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>128K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">130,244</td> <td style="text-align: right">130,246</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>256K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">260,444</td> <td style="text-align: right">260,446</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Both model headers declared a 262,144-token maximum context. The paired prompts differed by two tokens at every checkpoint.</p> <h3 id="median-post-warmup-generation-speed"> <a href="#median-post-warmup-generation-speed" title="Median post-warmup generation speed">Median post-warmup generation speed</a> <a href="#median-post-warmup-generation-speed" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Median post-warmup generation speed">#</a> </h3> <p>Each median covers five measured requests after one warmup. Every dense measured request reused all but four prompt tokens. Every Flash measured request reused all but seven prompt tokens. The table measures warm, prefix-cached decode throughput. The table does not measure cold end-to-end latency.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th style="text-align: right">Context</th> <th style="text-align: right">Flash IQ2_XS on Strata</th> <th style="text-align: right">Dense Q4_K_M on Ollama</th> <th style="text-align: right">Flash lead</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>4K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">98.4 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">65.0 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.51x</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>16K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">96.8 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">60.6 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.60x</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>32K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">95.3 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">64.4 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.48x</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>64K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">89.6 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">51.2 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.75x</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>128K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">92.9 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">31.5 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">2.95x</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>256K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">92.8 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.939 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">98.9x</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The Flash stack stayed near 90 tokens per second from 64K through 256K. Dense Qwen3.8 slowed sharply after 64K and reached 0.939 tokens per second at 256K. The 256K Flash response ended normally after 67 tokens. The dense run reached the 128-token output limit.</p> <h3 id="first-request-prompt-processing"> <a href="#first-request-prompt-processing" title="First-request prompt processing">First-request prompt processing</a> <a href="#first-request-prompt-processing" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="First-request prompt processing">#</a> </h3> <table> <thead> <tr> <th style="text-align: right">Context</th> <th style="text-align: right">Flash first request</th> <th style="text-align: right">Dense first request</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>4K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">1,134 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">832 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>16K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">2,013 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">856 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>32K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">2,386 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">799 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>64K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">2,509 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">690 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>128K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">2,538 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">489 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td style="text-align: right"><strong>256K</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">2,399 tok/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">214 tok/s</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The dense first request processed the full prompt at every checkpoint. Strata reported 16,384 reused prefix tokens at 64K, 49,152 at 128K, and 114,688 at 256K. Treat the 64K through 256K Flash rates as first-request continuation throughput, not fully uncached prefill.</p> <p>At 256K, Strata processed the first request in 60.8 seconds. Ollama took about 1,215.4 seconds. The prefix reuse prevents a direct cold-prefill comparison at this checkpoint.</p> <h3 id="runtime-placement-explains-the-long-context-split"> <a href="#runtime-placement-explains-the-long-context-split" title="Runtime placement explains the long-context split">Runtime placement explains the long-context split</a> <a href="#runtime-placement-explains-the-long-context-split" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Runtime placement explains the long-context split">#</a> </h3> <p>Ollama 0.34.2 used llama-server 0.4.1-dev with CUDA layer offload, the ChatML template, and MTP speculative decoding with a maximum draft width of four. Batch and microbatch sizes were 1,024 at 32K and 512 from 64K through 256K. All 66 dense layers stayed on the GPUs at 32K and 64K. At 128K, 63 of 66 layers stayed on the GPUs and 1,404 MiB moved to CPU-mapped memory. At 256K, 42 of 66 layers stayed on the GPUs and 6,002 MiB moved to CPU-mapped memory. The 256K MTP acceptance rate was about 69.4 percent.</p> <p>Strata 0.1.44.1 with CUDA 13.0.3 kept its 48 layers split across both GPUs. The 4K and 16K configuration placed layers 0 through 23 on the first GPU and layers 24 through 47 on the second. This pass used an automatic 700 MiB VRAM reserve and 16,047 resident expert slots.</p> <p>The 32K through 256K configuration placed layers 0 through 24 on the first GPU and layers 25 through 47 on the second. This pass used automatic prefill, a speculative minimum probability of 0.5, INT8 KV storage, 32,768 resident KV cells per QSA layer, an 832 MiB VRAM reserve, an expert cache with 15,318 slots and 21,024 MiB, and MTP speculative decoding with a maximum draft width of four.</p> <p>The Strata native and PLE blob digest was <code>sha256:1473e0664c2017095f9164b6d617d7a71893452c1180c83002c4f28fc8c2b0da</code>. The run also depended on an expert profile and an MTP draft pack without published immutable digests.</p> <p>The Strata run used the default route-tail skip mode. This setting slightly changes model output and makes the result specific to the recorded runtime configuration. Flash responses carried <code>BENCHMARK_OK</code> markers. The dense requests returned zero API errors, but the primary harness did not capture the marker. Its raw rows recorded zero response characters. A follow-up probe found output in response and thinking fields and confirmed <code>BENCHMARK_OK</code> in the response.</p> <p>The 4K and 16K configuration logged one request at 409 MiB free and recommended an 832 MiB reserve. The long-context configuration logged one request at 481 MiB free and recommended an 896 MiB reserve. Both values fell below the engine’s 512 MiB driver-paging threshold. No request failed, but these low-memory states affect repeatability.</p> <p><strong>Treat the 98.9x figure as a full-stack long-context result, not proof of a 98.9x engine-only advantage.</strong> The test isolates the host. The test does not isolate the model, quantization, or runtime.</p> <h2 id="actual-prompt-lengths-matter"> <a href="#actual-prompt-lengths-matter" title="Actual prompt lengths matter">Actual prompt lengths matter</a> <a href="#actual-prompt-lengths-matter" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Actual prompt lengths matter">#</a> </h2> <p>The requested context is not the same as the number of prompt tokens processed. At the 256K setting, the Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, Nemotron, and Qwen3.8 runs processed about 171,359 to 171,365 actual prompt tokens on both systems.</p> <p>GPT-OSS processed 65,538 actual prompt tokens at the 256K setting on both systems. Its 256K row therefore does not represent the same input length as the other models.</p> <p>The 256K Qwen3.8 result is the clearest split. The dual-card system processed 171,359 prompt tokens at 251.3 tokens per second and generated at 1.079 tokens per second. The GB10 processed the same number of prompt tokens at 535.1 tokens per second and generated at 22.371 tokens per second.</p> <p><strong>A context setting proves the requested limit.</strong> The actual prompt-token count proves the workload completed by the runtime.</p> <h2 id="why-aggregate-vram-still-matters"> <a href="#why-aggregate-vram-still-matters" title="Why aggregate VRAM still matters">Why aggregate VRAM still matters</a> <a href="#why-aggregate-vram-still-matters" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Why aggregate VRAM still matters">#</a> </h2> <h3 id="1-the-model-does-not-see-one-32-gb-card"> <a href="#1-the-model-does-not-see-one-32-gb-card" title="1. The model does not see one 32 GB card">1. The model does not see one 32 GB card</a> <a href="#1-the-model-does-not-see-one-32-gb-card" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="1. The model does not see one 32 GB card">#</a> </h3> <p>Two GPUs do not merge their memory into a single local address space. A model-parallel runtime divides layers or tensors across devices. Each device still needs room for its assigned weights, temporary buffers, and part of the context state.</p> <p>The usable capacity is lower than the simple sum suggests. The exact overhead depends on the model format, quantization, inference backend, tensor split, and context length.</p> <h3 id="2-context-memory-grows-during-generation"> <a href="#2-context-memory-grows-during-generation" title="2. Context memory grows during generation">2. Context memory grows during generation</a> <a href="#2-context-memory-grows-during-generation" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="2. Context memory grows during generation">#</a> </h3> <p>The model weights are only one part of the memory budget. The key-value cache, or KV cache, stores attention data for prior tokens. Longer contexts require more cache memory. A 4K test does not predict a 128K or 256K deployment.</p> <p>The new results show different failure points by model. Qwen3.8 suffers a severe generation collapse on the dual-card system at 256K. The other four models keep usable generation speed on both systems. Memory capacity remains important because it determines which model and context combinations fit with room for runtime allocations.</p> <h3 id="3-pcie-transfers-add-a-tax"> <a href="#3-pcie-transfers-add-a-tax" title="3. PCIe transfers add a tax">3. PCIe transfers add a tax</a> <a href="#3-pcie-transfers-add-a-tax" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="3. PCIe transfers add a tax">#</a> </h3> <p>When the runtime moves activations or tensors between GPUs, the transfer crosses the host interconnect. This creates synchronization points and adds latency to each step. The penalty depends on tensor placement, model architecture, quantization, and context length.</p> <p>This does not make a dual-GPU system useless. It means the runtime configuration and model determine the result. A benchmark reporting only prompt processing at 4K misses this cost.</p> <h3 id="4-power-efficiency-remains-a-system-level-advantage"> <a href="#4-power-efficiency-remains-a-system-level-advantage" title="4. Power efficiency remains a system-level advantage">4. Power efficiency remains a system-level advantage</a> <a href="#4-power-efficiency-remains-a-system-level-advantage" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="4. Power efficiency remains a system-level advantage">#</a> </h3> <p>The GB10 uses less reported chip or GPU power while providing more memory capacity. Two RTX 5060 Ti cards carry a 360 W combined GPU power figure before the rest of the system. NVIDIA lists the GB10 TDP at 140 W.</p> <p><strong>The GB10 trades peak throughput on several models for capacity, a shared working set, and lower reported GPU power.</strong> The dual-card system delivers higher measured throughput on several newer MoE models.</p> <h2 id="the-5060ti-x2-system-costs-far-less"> <a href="#the-5060ti-x2-system-costs-far-less" title="The 5060ti-x2 system costs far less">The 5060ti-x2 system costs far less</a> <a href="#the-5060ti-x2-system-costs-far-less" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The 5060ti-x2 system costs far less">#</a> </h2> <p>A complete dual RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB workstation was listed at <strong>$3,479</strong> on October 10, 2026. The configuration includes an Intel Ultra 7 265K, Z890 motherboard, 32 GB of DDR5, 1 TB storage, a 1,000 W power supply, and both GPUs. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="View the complete dual-GPU workstation listing"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://greenbeastgaming.com/products/dual-gpu-rtx-5060-ti-16gb-intel-focus-g-white"> <a href="https://greenbeastgaming.com/products/dual-gpu-rtx-5060-ti-16gb-intel-focus-g-white" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >View the complete dual-GPU workstation listing</a> </span> .</p> <p>NVIDIA’s US marketplace lists the 128 GB DGX Spark at <strong>$6,950</strong>. The listing includes 128 GB of coherent unified memory and 4 TB of NVMe storage, but shows the system as out of stock. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Check NVIDIA’s current DGX Spark listing"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://marketplace.nvidia.com/en-us/enterprise/personal-ai-supercomputers/dgx-spark/"> <a href="https://marketplace.nvidia.com/en-us/enterprise/personal-ai-supercomputers/dgx-spark/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Check NVIDIA’s current DGX Spark listing</a> </span> .</p> <p>The AMD Ryzen AI Halo Developer Platform provides another comparison point. This Strix Halo system lists for <strong>$3,999.99</strong> at Micro Center with 128 GB of LPDDR5x unified memory and 2 TB of storage. Strix Halo often lands in the same practical local-AI class as GB10 systems, although independent testing frequently measures GB10 ahead in throughput and software maturity. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Check the current Micro Center Linux listing"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.microcenter.com/product/711961/amd-ryzen-ai-halo-developer-platform?osfs=false"> <a href="https://www.microcenter.com/product/711961/amd-ryzen-ai-halo-developer-platform?osfs=false" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Check the current Micro Center Linux listing</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="read the Strix Halo versus GB10 review"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/embargo-mon-july-6-8am-pt-1100-edt-amd-ryzen-ai-halo-review/4"> <a href="https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/embargo-mon-july-6-8am-pt-1100-edt-amd-ryzen-ai-halo-review/4" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >read the Strix Halo versus GB10 review</a> </span> .</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Complete system</th> <th style="text-align: right">Listed price on October 10, 2026</th> <th style="text-align: right">Price difference</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>5060ti-x2 workstation</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">$3,479</td> <td style="text-align: right">Baseline</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>AMD Ryzen AI Halo, Strix Halo</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">$3,999.99</td> <td style="text-align: right">$520.99 more</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>128 GB GB10 DGX Spark</strong></td> <td style="text-align: right">$6,950</td> <td style="text-align: right">$3,471 more</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The GB10 provides a larger unified memory pool and lower reported GPU power. The AMD system provides the same 128 GB memory class for around $4,000. The 5060ti-x2 workstation remains about <strong>50% of the listed GB10 price</strong>, before tax and shipping.</p> <p>These are listed prices from different vendors, not a controlled retail basket. The comparison also leaves the 5060ti-x2 system with less system memory and storage. Current RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB card listings sit near <strong>$789 to $830 each</strong>, far above the $429 launch MSRP, so the dual-card price advantage survives during the current GPU price spike. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Current RTX 5060 Ti price checks"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.pcgamer.com/hardware/graphics-cards/graphics-card-price-watch-deals/"> <a href="https://www.pcgamer.com/hardware/graphics-cards/graphics-card-price-watch-deals/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Current RTX 5060 Ti price checks</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="what-this-means-for-local-ai-workloads"> <a href="#what-this-means-for-local-ai-workloads" title="What this means for local AI workloads">What this means for local AI workloads</a> <a href="#what-this-means-for-local-ai-workloads" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What this means for local AI workloads">#</a> </h2> <p>A two-card 16 GB setup runs several quantized 27B to 35B models at long context settings. The benchmark does not support a single winner for every model.</p> <p>Choose the dual-card system when you value:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Higher generation speed on GPT-OSS, Nemotron, Qwen3.5, and Qwen3.6</strong> in this test.</li> <li><strong>Higher short-context throughput</strong> across the five models.</li> <li><strong>Lower purchase cost</strong> than the listed GB10 system.</li> <li><strong>NVIDIA discrete-GPU software compatibility</strong> and future model experimentation.</li> </ul> <p>Choose the GB10 when you value:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Qwen3.8 27B at 256K</strong>, where the GB10 is over 20 times faster in generation.</li> <li><strong>A single 128 GB memory pool</strong> with more room for model weights, KV cache, and runtime buffers.</li> <li><strong>Lower reported GPU or chip power</strong> than two discrete cards.</li> <li><strong>Fewer multi-device placement constraints</strong> for models that stress the dual-card setup.</li> </ul> <p>This matches the sizing guidance in <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Is 16GB VRAM Enough for Serious Local LLM Work?"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/is-16gb-vram-enough-local-llm/"> <a href="/articles/is-16gb-vram-enough-local-llm/" rel="follow me" >Is 16GB VRAM Enough for Serious Local LLM Work?</a> </span> , which treats weights, context, and runtime allocations as one budget. The <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="32GB VRAM guide for Qwen 27B"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/32gb-vram-qwen-27b-hardware-guide/"> <a href="/articles/32gb-vram-qwen-27b-hardware-guide/" rel="follow me" >32GB VRAM guide for Qwen 27B</a> </span> reaches the same conclusion for two-card builds. Aggregate capacity does not equal usable headroom.</p> <p>For any long-context deployment, ask four questions before buying hardware:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Does the requested quantization fit with runtime buffers?</strong> Model weights alone do not define the memory requirement.</li> <li><strong>Does the context fit without severe KV-cache pressure?</strong> Long prompts change the result.</li> <li><strong>Does the runtime use an efficient device split?</strong> PCIe transfers and tensor placement affect every generated token.</li> <li><strong>Does the system complete the target context?</strong> A fast 4K result does not offset a failed 256K workload.</li> </ul> <p><strong>The new benchmark answers these questions by model.</strong> Qwen3.8 strongly favors the GB10 at 256K. The other four models favor the dual-card system for generation speed in this specific setup. The larger unified-memory pool still provides more capacity headroom, even when it does not deliver the highest measured throughput.</p> <p>The same dual-GPU hardware also recorded a 92.8-token-per-second post-warmup median at 256K with Flash-Next IQ2_XS on Strata. This separate result does not reverse the dense Qwen3.8 GB10 finding. Flash-Next uses a different mixture-of-experts architecture, quantization, package, runtime, and decode mode. No matched GB10 Flash-Next result exists in this dataset.</p> <h2 id="verdict"> <a href="#verdict" title="Verdict">Verdict</a> <a href="#verdict" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verdict">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>The dual RTX 5060 Ti system is faster for four of the five tested models at 256K generation.</strong> It also costs about half as much as the listed GB10 system. The GB10 remains the better choice for Qwen3.8 27B at 256K, for capacity headroom, and for workloads that benefit from one coherent memory pool.</p> <p>The earlier Qwen-only result suggested a simple GB10 win. The updated five-model run shows why that conclusion was too broad. Model architecture, runtime version, tensor placement, and context behavior affect the result.</p> <p>If you run GPT-OSS, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, Qwen3.5, or Qwen3.6, the dual-card system produced higher generation speed in this benchmark. If you run Qwen3.8 27B at 256K, the GB10 produced usable generation speed while the dual-card system nearly stalled.</p> <p><strong>Memory capacity and throughput are separate buying criteria.</strong> The GB10 offers four times the aggregate memory and a simpler shared working set. The dual-card system offers higher observed throughput on most tested models at a much lower listed system price.</p> <p>The Strata result adds a second lesson. Runtime placement, model architecture, and decode mode changed the 256K result on the same dual-card host. Flash-Next IQ2_XS kept a post-warmup median near 93 tokens per second while dense Qwen3.8 offloaded 24 layers and slowed below one token per second.</p> <h2 id="benchmark-limits"> <a href="#benchmark-limits" title="Benchmark limits">Benchmark limits</a> <a href="#benchmark-limits" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Benchmark limits">#</a> </h2> <p>The benchmark records the model tags, requested contexts, actual prompt tokens, prompt-processing speed, generation speed, Ollama versions, and the 128-token generation target. It does not record resolved manifest digests, CPU power, wall power, fan speed, or cooling setup.</p> <p>The GPT-OSS 256K rows processed 65,538 actual prompt tokens on both systems. The other 256K rows processed about 171K actual prompt tokens. Treat the figures as an observed system comparison, not a universal ranking of every RTX 5060 Ti pair and every GB10 implementation.</p> <p>The Strata versus dense run records exact prompt counts, five measured requests per context, runtime versions, device placement, cache settings, and request status. The comparison changes model architecture, quantization, packaging, runtime, and decode mode together. Strata also reused prompt prefixes above 32K. The measured generation requests on both stacks reused nearly the entire prompt.</p> <p>Exact reproduction from this article is unavailable. The benchmark harness, Strata pack layout, expert profile, and MTP draft pack are not published with immutable digests. The low-VRAM warning also adds run-to-run risk. The test isolates the host, not the inference engine.</p> <p>The hardware specifications above come from NVIDIA. The performance figures come from the controlled benchmark run for this article.</p> <h2 id="references"> <a href="#references" title="References">References</a> <a href="#references" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="References">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Ollama Qwen3.8 model library"> <meta itemprop="url"
