content="https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects"> <a href="https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Claude Projects</a> </span> before relying on a feature. The study route does not prove hands-on skill with an unavailable coding agent. Record the distinction in your completion notes.</p> <p><strong>Use one default path:</strong> ChatGPT in a browser for chat exercises, then one available coding agent with the local lab. Claude is an equivalent chat path. Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI, and OpenCode remain choices for the coding stage. You do not need accounts with every vendor.</p> <p><strong>Record a five-part preflight before opening a coding agent.</strong> This separates a local lab check from an account or hosted-workspace claim.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Check</th> <th>Record</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Workspace</strong></td> <td>Exact extracted lab folder the agent will read</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Execution</strong></td> <td>Local computer or selected remote workspace</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Provider</strong></td> <td>Account or model provider used for this task</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Permissions</strong></td> <td>File writes and shell commands allowed or subject to approval</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Baseline</strong></td> <td>Observed count and two passing tests before edits</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Keep the practice root narrow.</strong> A hosted workspace needs its own copy of the synthetic lab. A local run does not prove the remote copy or account has the same files and permissions.</p> <h2 id="learn-the-local-terms"> <a href="#learn-the-local-terms" title="Learn the Local Terms">Learn the Local Terms</a> <a href="#learn-the-local-terms" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Learn the Local Terms">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Term</th> <th>Plain meaning</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Terminal</strong></td> <td>An app where you type commands</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Shell</strong></td> <td>Software interpreting those commands</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>CLI</strong></td> <td>A command line interface to a program</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Working directory</strong></td> <td>The folder a command uses by default</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Repository</strong></td> <td>A project tracked by Git</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Commit</strong></td> <td>A saved Git snapshot</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Branch</strong></td> <td>A named line of Git changes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Diff</strong></td> <td>A display of lines added or removed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Test</strong></td> <td>A repeatable check of expected behavior</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Exit code</strong></td> <td>A number reporting command success or failure</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>You do not need GitHub for the starter lab.</strong> Git works on your computer. GitHub is a separate hosting service. A local commit records a snapshot without sending your files anywhere.</p> <h2 id="prepare-the-lab"> <a href="#prepare-the-lab" title="Prepare the Lab">Prepare the Lab</a> <a href="#prepare-the-lab" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Prepare the Lab">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Download the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="course starter lab"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/downloads/effective-ai-course-lab.zip"> <a href="/downloads/effective-ai-course-lab.zip" rel="follow me" >course starter lab</a> </span> </strong> and extract it into a new folder you control. Open a terminal in the folder. On macOS or Linux, use Terminal and <code>cd</code> to enter the extracted directory. On Windows, use PowerShell or Windows Terminal and <code>cd</code> to enter the folder. The Python command on Windows is often <code>py -3</code> instead of <code>python3</code>.</p> <p><strong>Install <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Python 3.10 or later"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.python.org/downloads/"> <a href="https://www.python.org/downloads/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Python 3.10 or later</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Git"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://git-scm.com/downloads"> <a href="https://git-scm.com/downloads" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Git</a> </span> if needed.</strong> Check the installed tools before running the lab. The first two commands print version numbers. <code>cd</code> changes the working directory. <code>ls</code> lists files. Replace the example folder path with your extracted folder’s actual path.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 --version </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git --version </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cd /path/to/effective-ai-course-lab </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ls </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>On Windows PowerShell,</strong> use <code>py -3 --version</code>, <code>git --version</code>, <code>cd C:\path\to\effective-ai-course-lab</code>, and <code>Get-ChildItem</code>. The listed files should include <code>task_report.py</code>, <code>tasks.json</code>, <code>tests</code>, and <code>docs</code>. If a version command fails, finish the installation before continuing.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>pwd </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 task_report.py tasks.json </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>On Windows PowerShell,</strong> replace <code>pwd</code> with <code>Get-Location</code> if you prefer, and replace <code>python3</code> with <code>py -3</code> when Python uses the launcher. Read the path from the first command. It should end in your extracted lab folder. Check the filenames too. A file saved as <code>AGENTS.md.txt</code> will not serve as <code>AGENTS.md</code>. In Windows Explorer, turn on file name extensions to inspect the full name.</p> <p><strong>Expected output:</strong> the report says <code>Total tasks: 4</code>. The test command names two tests and ends with <code>OK</code>. A shell returns exit code zero after success. A different count or a traceback means you should stop and inspect the folder and Python setup.</p> <p><strong>Read each command as parts.</strong> In <code>python3 task_report.py tasks.json</code>, <code>python3</code> launches Python, <code>task_report.py</code> is the program, and <code>tasks.json</code> is an argument naming input data. The printed count is output, not another command. After a failed command, macOS and Linux show its status with <code>echo $?</code>. PowerShell exposes the last native program status through <code>$LASTEXITCODE</code>.</p> <p><strong>Plan about ten minutes for the first run</strong> once Python is installed: extract the lab, run the report, and match the count to the four entries in <code>tasks.json</code>. Open the JSON file in a text editor and count the entries yourself.</p> <h2 id="practice-git-safely"> <a href="#practice-git-safely" title="Practice Git Safely">Practice Git Safely</a> <a href="#practice-git-safely" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Practice Git Safely">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start Git only inside the extracted lab folder.</strong> The commands below make a local snapshot. The <code>git status</code> command shows whether files changed. The <code>git diff</code> command shows changed lines after you edit a tracked file.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>git init </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git add . </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git commit -m <span style="color:#e6db74">"Baseline course lab"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git status --short </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Expected status:</strong> no file names appear after the commit. If Git asks for a name and email, set a lab-only identity from inside this folder, then rerun the commit. Replace the example values with your own private values. Do not paste identity or credential output into a public chat.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>git config --local user.name <span style="color:#e6db74">"Course Learner"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git config --local user.email <span style="color:#e6db74">"learner@example.invalid"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git commit -m <span style="color:#e6db74">"Baseline course lab"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>git status --short </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>A reset needs no Git command.</strong> Save notes outside the lab, delete the extracted practice copy, and extract the original ZIP again. Use this reset when a lesson’s edit leaves the program in an unknown state.</p> <h2 id="protect-your-practice-space"> <a href="#protect-your-practice-space" title="Protect Your Practice Space">Protect Your Practice Space</a> <a href="#protect-your-practice-space" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Protect Your Practice Space">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Use synthetic examples.</strong> Do not upload private documents to a course project. Do not put API keys in prompts, source files, screenshots, or commits. A coding agent’s file and command access depends on its permissions and the folder you open. Inspect both before letting it run.</p> <p><strong>Check sharing before upload.</strong> Project files might be available to project members. Follow your organization’s policy for real work. The course uses fictional data so you need no special approval for the lab itself.</p> <h2 id="practice-and-check"> <a href="#practice-and-check" title="Practice and Check">Practice and Check</a> <a href="#practice-and-check" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Practice and Check">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Your artifact:</strong> record your chosen route, the five preflight fields, the report count, the test result, and the reset method. Use a fresh lab copy to confirm you know how to reset.</p> <p><strong>Expected reasoning:</strong> you know which folder commands affect, you distinguish local Git from hosting, and you have a way to recover before an agent edits files.</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Question:</strong> Does a browser-only introduction complete the local lab route? <strong>Answer:</strong> No. The complete route requires a local Python and Git baseline.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Question:</strong> What should you save before changing the disposable lab? <strong>Answer:</strong> The passing starter test result and a clean reset point.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Python command missing:</strong> install Python 3 from its official distributor, then reopen the terminal.</li> <li><strong>File not found:</strong> check the working directory and list the extracted folder’s files.</li> <li><strong>Tests do not run:</strong> use the exact command from the lab README in the extracted folder.</li> <li><strong>Git commit asks for identity:</strong> configure Git locally and keep the chosen values out of course notes.</li> </ul> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Continue with <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="the Reliable AI Workflow"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-workflow-foundations/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-workflow-foundations/" rel="follow me" >the Reliable AI Workflow</a> </span> </strong>. The first exercise uses the same synthetic workshop before any tool receives real files.</p> <p><strong>Course navigation:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Course outline"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/effective-ai-course-start/"> <a href="/effective-ai-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Course outline</a> </span> .</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Bounded AI Agent Loops: Checks, Retries, and Stop Rules
item.description: Define an AI goal loop with observable state, checks, retry limits, stop conditions, and a clear human handoff.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the Practical AI Workflow Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/effective-ai-course-start/"> <a href="/effective-ai-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Return to the Practical AI Workflow Course</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>A goal loop repeats work until a defined result passes or a stop rule fires.</strong> The useful loop reads current state, takes one bounded action, checks the result, and records what happened. An open-ended “keep trying” instruction has no reliable completion rule.</p> <p><strong>Learning outcome:</strong> you will run a bounded lab loop with a known failed check and record its stop decision.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Goal:</strong> a result stated in observable terms.</li> <li><strong>State:</strong> the current files, outputs, errors, and source revision.</li> <li><strong>Check:</strong> a test or review tied to the goal.</li> <li><strong>Retry budget:</strong> the maximum attempts allowed for one failure.</li> <li><strong>Stop rule:</strong> a condition requiring an end or human decision.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Prerequisites:</strong> the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="task packet"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-task-packets/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-task-packets/" rel="follow me" >task packet</a> </span> , <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="verification record"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-output-verification/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-output-verification/" rel="follow me" >verification record</a> </span> , and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="delegation lesson"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-agent-delegation/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-agent-delegation/" rel="follow me" >delegation lesson</a> </span> . Set aside 45 minutes. Difficulty is intermediate. Use a fresh copy of the synthetic lab so the first failed check is known in advance.</p> <h2 id="write-the-loop-contract"> <a href="#write-the-loop-contract" title="Write the Loop Contract">Write the Loop Contract</a> <a href="#write-the-loop-contract" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Write the Loop Contract">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>For the status-filter request,</strong> set the contract before any retry:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Goal: support --status open|done without changing default output. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Source: docs/requirements.md, revision 1. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Allowed files: task_report.py and focused tests. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Checks: unit tests, counts 4/2/2, invalid value exits nonzero. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Retry budget: at most two edits after the first attempt. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Stop immediately: source conflict, unexpected file change, secret exposure, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>or a failing baseline unrelated to this request. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Handoff: report final diff, commands, outputs, attempts, and unresolved issue. </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>The budget is a task policy,</strong> not a product default. Two retries are enough to diagnose a small lab task without hiding repeated failure. A production task needs its own risk and review choice.</p> <h2 id="use-a-state-table"> <a href="#use-a-state-table" title="Use a State Table">Use a State Table</a> <a href="#use-a-state-table" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Use a State Table">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Step</th> <th>State to record</th> <th>Decision</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Read</strong></td> <td>Source revision and baseline result</td> <td>Stop if the starting state differs</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Act</strong></td> <td>Changed files and action taken</td> <td>Reject out-of-scope edits</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Check</strong></td> <td>Exact test and manual output</td> <td>Accept or diagnose</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Retry</strong></td> <td>Failure cause and new hypothesis</td> <td>Continue only within budget</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Handoff</strong></td> <td>Final state and next owner</td> <td>Stop after pass or blocked result</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>Record attempts, not only the last message.</strong> A test passing after three hidden edits leaves no useful account of what changed. Keep a short attempt log with the failure, revised hypothesis, and new evidence.</p> <h2 id="walk-through-a-failure"> <a href="#walk-through-a-failure" title="Walk Through a Failure">Walk Through a Failure</a> <a href="#walk-through-a-failure" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Walk Through a Failure">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Illustrative first attempt:</strong> the agent adds filtering and tests. <code>open</code> prints 2, but <code>--status invalid</code> prints 0 and exits successfully. The requirement says an invalid value needs a nonzero exit. Mark the check failed.</p> <p><strong>Diagnosis:</strong> inspect argument validation. The agent treated an unknown value as an empty match instead of an error. Ask for one scoped fix to validate accepted values before counting. Run the same invalid case and all earlier checks again.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Attempt 1: invalid status returned success, so acceptance failed. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Cause found: no accepted-value validation. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Attempt 2 request: reject unsupported values and retain 4/2/2 counts. </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Evidence required: full test run and invalid command exit status. </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Expected second result:</strong> a clear error and nonzero status for <code>invalid</code>, with unchanged valid counts. If the second run still fails, use the remaining retry only after naming a new cause. Repeating the same prompt is not diagnosis.</p> <h2 id="handle-ambiguous-results"> <a href="#handle-ambiguous-results" title="Handle Ambiguous Results">Handle Ambiguous Results</a> <a href="#handle-ambiguous-results" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Handle Ambiguous Results">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>A process stopping without a result is not success.</strong> If a tool times out after a possible file write, inspect the files and Git status before rerunning it. If a connected service reports an unknown outcome, read its current state before retrying an external action. Duplicate sends, posts, or writes are a real risk outside the lab.</p> <p><strong>Stop for human review</strong> when the requirement conflicts with another approved source, a permission blocks the action, the retry budget ends, or the requested action crosses a publication boundary. The handoff should name the exact state and the choice needed.</p> <h2 id="separate-loops-from-monitors"> <a href="#separate-loops-from-monitors" title="Separate Loops from Monitors">Separate Loops from Monitors</a> <a href="#separate-loops-from-monitors" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Separate Loops from Monitors">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>An edit loop</strong> runs within a bounded task and checks after each action. <strong>A scheduled monitor</strong> wakes later to inspect a condition. A monitor needs its own cadence, change threshold, notification rule, and stop condition. Do not turn the lab edit loop into a recurring job. The next lesson evaluates persistent systems before enabling them.</p> <h2 id="run-a-controlled-loop"> <a href="#run-a-controlled-loop" title="Run a Controlled Loop">Run a Controlled Loop</a> <a href="#run-a-controlled-loop" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Run a Controlled Loop">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Start with the untouched lab.</strong> Its two baseline tests pass. Create <code>tests/test_loop_contract.py</code> in the fresh extraction with the check below. This file states a desired feature absent from the starter. It does not belong in the maintained starter ZIP.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-python" data-lang="python"><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">"""One controlled failing check for the status-filter exercise."""</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">import</span> subprocess </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">import</span> sys </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">import</span> unittest </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#f92672">from</span> pathlib <span style="color:#f92672">import</span> Path </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ROOT <span style="color:#f92672">=</span> Path(__file__)<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>resolve()<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>parents[<span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span>] </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">class</span> <span style="color:#a6e22e">LoopContractTests</span>(unittest<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>TestCase): </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">def</span> <span style="color:#a6e22e">test_open_status_count</span>(self): </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> result <span style="color:#f92672">=</span> subprocess<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>run( </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> [sys<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>executable, str(ROOT <span style="color:#f92672">/</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"task_report.py"</span>), </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> str(ROOT <span style="color:#f92672">/</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"tasks.json"</span>), <span style="color:#e6db74">"--status"</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">"open"</span>], </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> capture_output<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#66d9ef">True</span>, text<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#66d9ef">True</span>, check<span style="color:#f92672">=</span><span style="color:#66d9ef">False</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> ) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> self<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>assertEqual(result<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>returncode, <span style="color:#ae81ff">0</span>, result<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>stderr) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> self<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>assertEqual(result<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>stdout<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>strip(), <span style="color:#e6db74">"Total tasks: 2"</span>) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> __name__ <span style="color:#f92672">==</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"__main__"</span>: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> unittest<span style="color:#f92672">.</span>main() </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>Run <code>python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v</code>.</strong> The two original tests should pass and the new contract test should fail because the starter lacks <code>--status</code>. Record the actual failure. If you initialized Git as shown in lesson 0, record <code>git status --short</code> too. Otherwise, compare changed files against an untouched extraction. On Windows, use <code>py -3</code> if your setup used the launcher.</p> <p><strong>Set an action budget of three attempts:</strong> the first edit plus at most two corrections. Give your agent the loop contract above and ask for one scoped edit. After each attempt, inspect changed files, rerun all tests, and run the default, open, done, and invalid commands. Record the failure cause before another edit. Stop on a pass, an unrelated baseline failure, an out-of-scope change, or the third failed action.</p> <p><strong>Study route:</strong> apply the complete <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="lesson 5 answer key"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-coding-agent-first-task/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-coding-agent-first-task/" rel="follow me" >lesson 5 answer key</a> </span> in this fresh copy after recording the red test. Rerun the same checks and mark the agent edit not run. Keep the controlled contract test. Do not weaken or delete it to make the loop pass.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Attempt</th> <th>State and observation</th> <th>Decision</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Before edit</strong></td> <td>Two baseline tests pass, new open check fails</td> <td>Proceed with one bounded edit</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>After each edit</strong></td> <td>Record exact tests, counts, invalid exit, changed files</td> <td>Accept, diagnose, or stop</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>At budget end</strong></td> <td>Record remaining failure and current diff</td> <td>Handoff without another retry</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="practice-and-check"> <a href="#practice-and-check" title="Practice and Check">Practice and Check</a> <a href="#practice-and-check" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Practice and Check">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Your artifact:</strong> the controlled failing test, observed before and after test output, an attempt log, and a final accept or stop handoff. If the first edit passes, record one attempt. Do not invent a second failure to fill a log.</p> <p><strong>Completion check:</strong> the contract names a source, file scope, observable checks, retry limit, at least one immediate stop condition, and a handoff. Your record includes the real red test, the later check results, and either a passing result or a budget stop. A second attempt names a new cause and differs from the first.</p> <h2 id="check-your-understanding"> <a href="#check-your-understanding" title="Check Your Understanding">Check Your Understanding</a> <a href="#check-your-understanding" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check Your Understanding">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li> <p><strong>Question:</strong> What does the first red contract test prove? <strong>Answer:</strong> The starter lacks the requested status filter under a test written before the edit.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Question:</strong> When must the loop stop even with retries left? <strong>Answer:</strong> Stop for an out-of-scope change, unclear permission, or conflicting requirement.</p> </li> </ol> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Loop repeats the same failure:</strong> stop and form a new cause hypothesis.</li> <li><strong>Checks become weaker:</strong> restore the original acceptance checks.</li> <li><strong>Uncertain external result:</strong> inspect current state before another action.</li> <li><strong>Budget exhausted:</strong> hand off the failure record instead of hiding it.</li> </ul> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Continue with <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Specialized Agent Evaluation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-specialized-agent-evaluation/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-specialized-agent-evaluation/" rel="follow me" >Specialized Agent Evaluation</a> </span> </strong> for the optional lesson, or go straight to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="AI Workflow Capstone"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-capstone/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-capstone/" rel="follow me" >AI Workflow Capstone</a> </span> . For broader runtime choices, read the site’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="agent runtime guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/best-ai-agent-harnesses/"> <a href="/articles/best-ai-agent-harnesses/" rel="follow me" >agent runtime guide</a> </span> .</p> <p><strong>Course navigation:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Previous: Agent Delegation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/effective-ai-agent-delegation/"> <a href="/articles/effective-ai-agent-delegation/" rel="follow me" >Previous: Agent Delegation</a> </span> , <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Course outline"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/effective-ai-course-start/"> <a href="/effective-ai-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Course outline</a> </span> .</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Build a Read-Only Active Directory Inventory With PowerShell
item.description: Inventory Active Directory OUs, users, and computers with scoped PowerShell queries. Export reviewable CSV files without changing directory objects.
item.content:encoded: <p>An Active Directory cleanup starts with a trustworthy list of what exists. This <strong>read-only inventory</strong> gathers organizational units, users, and computers from one chosen scope. It exports three comma-separated values (CSV) files for review without changing directory objects. You still need to protect those files because names and device details reveal part of your environment.</p> <h2 id="key-takeaways"> <a href="#key-takeaways" title="Key Takeaways">Key Takeaways</a> <a href="#key-takeaways" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Key Takeaways">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Choose a scope:</strong> Query one organizational unit before expanding to a whole domain.</li> <li><strong>Use read commands:</strong> <code>Get-ADOrganizationalUnit</code>, <code>Get-ADUser</code>, and <code>Get-ADComputer</code> retrieve objects.</li> <li><strong>Select fields:</strong> Export only the properties needed for the task.</li> <li><strong>Check the output:</strong> Compare counts and sample rows before relying on a report.</li> </ul> <h2 id="before-you-begin"> <a href="#before-you-begin" title="Before You Begin">Before You Begin</a> <a href="#before-you-begin" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Before You Begin">#</a> </h2> <p>You need a Windows administration host with working DNS and network access to a domain controller, the <strong>ActiveDirectory</strong> PowerShell module, an account approved to read the selected objects, and a protected folder for CSV output. On a Windows client, the module comes from the Active Directory tools in Remote Server Administration Tools (RSAT). The site’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Active Directory module guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/active-directory-module-powershell-installation-usage-guide/"> <a href="/articles/active-directory-module-powershell-installation-usage-guide/" rel="follow me" >Active Directory module guide</a> </span> covers installation. Microsoft lists the module’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="cmdlet reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >cmdlet reference</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="RSAT installation options"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/remote/remote-server-administration-tools"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/remote/remote-server-administration-tools" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >RSAT installation options</a> </span> . This guide uses Windows PowerShell syntax and avoids changes to directory objects.</p> <p>Directory permissions still apply. Microsoft explains that object access control lists often give authenticated users read access to general information while restricting sensitive fields and changes in its <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="privileged accounts guidance"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/security-best-practices/appendix-b--privileged-accounts-and-groups-in-active-directory"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/security-best-practices/appendix-b--privileged-accounts-and-groups-in-active-directory" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >privileged accounts guidance</a> </span> . Use an approved account and a test OU first. Do not elevate to Domain Admin to make an inventory succeed.</p> <blockquote> <p><strong>Warning:</strong> The CSV files contain account and computer names. Save them to an approved location, limit access, and remove extra copies after review. Do not publish a raw export or attach one to a public issue.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="choose-the-search-base"> <a href="#choose-the-search-base" title="Choose the Search Base">Choose the Search Base</a> <a href="#choose-the-search-base" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose the Search Base">#</a> </h2> <p>An <strong>organizational unit (OU)</strong> groups directory objects. Its <strong>distinguished name (DN)</strong> identifies its position in the directory tree. The <code>-SearchBase</code> parameter limits a query to a chosen DN. Without a deliberate scope, a broad filter might return far more objects than your review needs.</p> <p>First load the module and inspect the current domain DN:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Import-Module ActiveDirectory </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>(Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Microsoft documents <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Get-ADDomain"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-addomain"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-addomain" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Get-ADDomain</a> </span> and its domain output. Find the OU you intend to review before setting the search base:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter * -SearchBase (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Select-Object Name, DistinguishedName </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Copy the exact DN from the result. For the remaining examples, replace this documentation value with your OU’s DN:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$SearchBase = <span style="color:#e6db74">'OU=Lab,DC=example,DC=com'</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><code>example.com</code> is a documentation domain. Do not copy its DN into a live query. If you intentionally need a domain-wide inventory, set <code>$SearchBase</code> to the domain DN and record that broader scope in the report. Microsoft’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Get-ADOrganizationalUnit reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-adorganizationalunit"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-adorganizationalunit" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Get-ADOrganizationalUnit reference</a> </span> documents <code>-Filter</code> and <code>-SearchBase</code>.</p> <h2 id="inventory-ous-users-and-computers"> <a href="#inventory-ous-users-and-computers" title="Inventory OUs, Users, and Computers">Inventory OUs, Users, and Computers</a> <a href="#inventory-ous-users-and-computers" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Inventory OUs, Users, and Computers">#</a> </h2> <p>Start with counts. They give you a quick way to catch a wrong search base or unexpected empty result:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase | Measure-Object </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADUser -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase | Measure-Object </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADComputer -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase | Measure-Object </span></span></code></pre></div><p><code>-Filter *</code> means all matching objects within the search base. Microsoft documents <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Get-ADUser"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-aduser"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-aduser" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Get-ADUser</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Get-ADComputer"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-adcomputer"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-adcomputer" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Get-ADComputer</a> </span> as retrieval commands. A zero count might be legitimate, but check the DN, permissions, and target domain before treating it as a complete inventory.</p> <p>Now preview a few rows in the console. Store the selected fields so the preview and later CSV export use the same columns:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$UserFields = <span style="color:#e6db74">'Name'</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">'SamAccountName'</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">'Enabled'</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">'DistinguishedName'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADUser -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Select-Object -Property $UserFields -First <span style="color:#ae81ff">10</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p>For computers, request the extra operating system field only when your review needs it:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>$ComputerFields = @( </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'Name'</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">'DNSHostName'</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">'OperatingSystem'</span>, </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> <span style="color:#e6db74">'Enabled'</span>, <span style="color:#e6db74">'DistinguishedName'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>) </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADComputer -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase -Properties OperatingSystem | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Select-Object -Property $ComputerFields -First <span style="color:#ae81ff">10</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p>The <code>-Properties</code> parameter requests properties outside the cmdlet’s default set. Microsoft’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="computer cmdlet reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-adcomputer"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-adcomputer" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >computer cmdlet reference</a> </span> documents it. Treat operating system names as directory data, not proof of the current installed version. A computer object might be stale or its attribute might not have updated.</p> <h2 id="export-a-reviewable-csv"> <a href="#export-a-reviewable-csv" title="Export a Reviewable CSV">Export a Reviewable CSV</a> <a href="#export-a-reviewable-csv" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Export a Reviewable CSV">#</a> </h2> <p>Choose an approved output folder with enough space. The following commands write <strong>local CSV files</strong> and leave directory objects unchanged. Run them in that folder. <code>-NoClobber</code> prevents an existing file from being overwritten. Use a new folder or filename for each run.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-powershell" data-lang="powershell"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Select-Object Name, DistinguishedName | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Export-Csv -Path .\ad-ous.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 -NoClobber </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADUser -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Select-Object -Property $UserFields | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Export-Csv -Path .\ad-users.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 -NoClobber </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Get-ADComputer -Filter * -SearchBase $SearchBase -Properties OperatingSystem | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Select-Object -Property $ComputerFields | </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> Export-Csv -Path .\ad-computers.csv -NoTypeInformation -Encoding UTF8 -NoClobber </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Microsoft’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Export-Csv reference"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/export-csv?view=powershell-5.1"> <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/export-csv?view=powershell-5.1" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Export-Csv reference</a> </span> explains <code>-NoTypeInformation</code>, <code>-Encoding</code>, and <code>-NoClobber</code>. Open each CSV in a text editor or approved spreadsheet tool. Check its header, a few rows, and the number of records against the earlier counts. A failed command or a zero-byte file does not establish a complete report.</p> <blockquote> <p><strong>Expected Result:</strong> You have three scoped CSV files with OU, user, and computer records. Their row counts and sample entries match the selected directory scope.</p> </blockquote> <h2 id="review-without-changing-objects"> <a href="#review-without-changing-objects" title="Review Without Changing Objects">Review Without Changing Objects</a> <a href="#review-without-changing-objects" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Review Without Changing Objects">#</a> </h2> <p>Use the inventory to ask specific questions: Which OU owns a computer? Which users are disabled? Which device names need an owner? Record findings in a separate review note. Do not equate an <code>Enabled</code> value with whether an account is still needed. Do not delete or disable an object based on an export alone.</p> <p>For a recurring report, record the query date, domain, OU DN, selected properties, operator, and CSV location. If you compare two exports, confirm that both used the same scope and fields. Otherwise a difference might come from the query rather than an actual directory change.</p> <p>This is an <strong>inventory</strong>, not a privileged-account audit or a login-activity report. Microsoft notes that Active Directory properties and permissions vary by object and environment. An operating system attribute or display name should be verified with the system owner before you act on it. The site’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Active Directory security guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/active-directory-security-best-practices/"> <a href="/articles/active-directory-security-best-practices/" rel="follow me" >Active Directory security guide</a> </span> covers the broader security controls.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Module will not import:</strong> Confirm the Active Directory tools from RSAT or the Windows Server administration tools are installed on the host. Follow the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="module setup guide"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/active-directory-module-powershell-installation-usage-guide/"> <a href="/articles/active-directory-module-powershell-installation-usage-guide/" rel="follow me" >module setup guide</a> </span> .</li> <li><strong>Query returns no objects:</strong> Check the exact DN, current domain, OU contents, and read permissions. Try a known small OU before broadening scope.</li> <li><strong>A property is blank:</strong> Confirm that the attribute exists and that your account can read it. Do not fill missing fields with guesses.</li> <li><strong>Export says the file exists:</strong> <code>-NoClobber</code> protected the earlier report. Choose a new filename or folder and rerun.</li> <li><strong>Counts differ from expectations:</strong> Check whether users or computers sit in another OU, whether your scope changed, and whether the directory changed during the query.</li> </ul> <h2 id="next-steps"> <a href="#next-steps" title="Next Steps">Next Steps</a> <a href="#next-steps" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Next Steps">#</a> </h2> <p>Keep the raw CSV in a protected location for the agreed review period. Share only the fields the reviewer needs. After owners verify findings, plan changes through your normal approval and rollback process. Repeat the same scoped inventory after the approved changes to confirm the result.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Capstone: Plan and Validate a Secure Local AI Server
item.description: Produce a deployment package for a measured, access-controlled, monitored, and recoverable local AI server.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the Local AI Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course-start/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Return to the Local AI Course</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Your capstone produces a deployment decision, not a running public service.</strong> Use your measured host and model data. Keep tests on loopback or an approved private lab network.</p> <h2 id="choose-a-track"> <a href="#choose-a-track" title="Choose a Track">Choose a Track</a> <a href="#choose-a-track" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Choose a Track">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Beginner track:</strong> One user on one host. The runtime stays on loopback. The package proves model identity, acceptable task output, measured memory, local API access, and update rollback.</p> <p><strong>Advanced track:</strong> Several approved users on a private network. The runtime stays on loopback behind an authenticated TLS gateway. The package adds per-user authorization, rate limits, concurrency limits, monitoring, backup, staged updates, and access-denial evidence.</p> <h2 id="required-package"> <a href="#required-package" title="Required Package">Required Package</a> <a href="#required-package" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Required Package">#</a> </h2> <p>Create <strong><code>local-ai-capstone/</code></strong>:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>local-ai-capstone/ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> workload.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> host-inventory.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> model-record.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> benchmark.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> data-flow.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> access-policy.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> test-record.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> update-rollback.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> deployment-decision.md </span></span></code></pre></div><h2 id="build-the-package"> <a href="#build-the-package" title="Build the Package">Build the Package</a> <a href="#build-the-package" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build the Package">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li><strong>Freeze the workload.</strong> State input size, output size, users, latency target, and data class.</li> <li><strong>Record the host.</strong> Include CPU, RAM, GPU, VRAM, storage, operating system, and runtime version.</li> <li><strong>Identify the model.</strong> Include publisher, source, license, exact identifier, format, size, and digest where available.</li> <li><strong>Measure the service.</strong> Record three warm trials with separate prompt and generation rates.</li> <li><strong>Draw data flow.</strong> Show client, gateway, runtime, model storage, logs, updates, and outbound connections.</li> <li><strong>Write access policy.</strong> Name identities, routes, models, request limits, rate limits, and retention.</li> <li><strong>Run boundary tests.</strong> For the one-host beginner path, inspect the listener and record its <code>127.0.0.1</code> bind plus local firewall rules. A second private client is optional for a remote-denial test. For the advanced path, use the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="tested gateway lab source"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/downloads/local-ai-secure-server-course/secure_gateway_lab.py"> <a href="/downloads/local-ai-secure-server-course/secure_gateway_lab.py" rel="follow me" >tested gateway lab source</a> </span> from Lesson 5 to test authorized, unauthorized, oversized, unexpected-path, response-size, and rate-limit behavior. Inspect both loopback listeners. Test timeout and concurrency overload on your own approved gateway. The advanced capstone is incomplete until those two observed results exist. Separate synthetic lab evidence from server evidence.</li> <li><strong>Test rollback.</strong> Restore a prior approved configuration in the lab and repeat health and denial checks.</li> <li><strong>Make a decision.</strong> Choose approve, approve with conditions, or reject.</li> </ol> <h3 id="beginner-rollback-drill"> <a href="#beginner-rollback-drill" title="Beginner Rollback Drill">Beginner Rollback Drill</a> <a href="#beginner-rollback-drill" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Beginner Rollback Drill">#</a> </h3> <p>Use the course gateway lab for a concrete rollback drill. It uses fixed loopback ports and synthetic responses. For your own runtime, repeat the same checks with its documented service command.</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>mkdir -p local-ai-rollback </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cp secure_gateway_lab.py local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.before.py </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cp secure_gateway_lab.py local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.py </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>hash_file<span style="color:#f92672">()</span> <span style="color:#f92672">{</span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; <span style="color:#66d9ef">then</span> sha256sum <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$1<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>; <span style="color:#66d9ef">else</span> shasum -a <span style="color:#ae81ff">256</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$1<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>; <span style="color:#66d9ef">fi</span>; <span style="color:#f92672">}</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>check_listeners<span style="color:#f92672">()</span> <span style="color:#f92672">{</span> <span style="color:#66d9ef">if</span> command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; <span style="color:#66d9ef">then</span> ss -ltn | grep -E <span style="color:#e6db74">':(18080|18443) '</span>; <span style="color:#66d9ef">else</span> lsof -nP -iTCP:18080 -sTCP:LISTEN; lsof -nP -iTCP:18443 -sTCP:LISTEN; <span style="color:#66d9ef">fi</span>; <span style="color:#f92672">}</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#75715e"># On macOS, the fallback above uses /usr/bin/shasum and /usr/sbin/lsof.</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>hash_file local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.before.py </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 - <span style="color:#e6db74"><<'PY' </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">from pathlib import Path </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">path = Path("local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.py") </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">text = path.read_text() </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">path.write_text(text.replace("MAX_BODY = 512", "MAX_BODY = 256", 1)) </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">PY</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.py > local-ai-rollback/changed.log 2>&<span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span> & </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>LAB_PID<span style="color:#f92672">=</span>$! </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>trap <span style="color:#e6db74">'kill "$LAB_PID" 2>/dev/null || true'</span> EXIT </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sleep <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p>The controlled change lowers the request limit from 512 to 256 bytes. Record the changed health response, listener addresses, and unauthorized request result:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl -s -o /dev/null -w <span style="color:#e6db74">'%{http_code}\n'</span> http://127.0.0.1:18443/api/chat <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -H <span style="color:#e6db74">'Authorization: Bearer FAKE_LOCAL_AI_LAB_TOKEN'</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -H <span style="color:#e6db74">'Content-Type: application/json'</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -d <span style="color:#e6db74">'{"message":"READY"}'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>check_listeners </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl -s -o /dev/null -w <span style="color:#e6db74">'%{http_code}\n'</span> http://127.0.0.1:18443/api/chat <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -H <span style="color:#e6db74">'Content-Type: application/json'</span> -d <span style="color:#e6db74">'{"message":"READY"}'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 - <span style="color:#e6db74"><<'PY' | curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:18443/api/chat \ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74"> -H 'Authorization: Bearer FAKE_LOCAL_AI_LAB_TOKEN' \ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74"> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">import json </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">print(json.dumps({"message": "A" * 400})) </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">PY</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>kill <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$LAB_PID<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>wait <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$LAB_PID<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> 2>/dev/null <span style="color:#f92672">||</span> true </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cp local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.before.py local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.py </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>hash_file local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.py </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 local-ai-rollback/secure_gateway_lab.py > local-ai-rollback/restored.log 2>&<span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span> & </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>LAB_PID<span style="color:#f92672">=</span>$! </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>sleep <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl -s -o /dev/null -w <span style="color:#e6db74">'%{http_code}\n'</span> http://127.0.0.1:18443/api/chat <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -H <span style="color:#e6db74">'Authorization: Bearer FAKE_LOCAL_AI_LAB_TOKEN'</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -H <span style="color:#e6db74">'Content-Type: application/json'</span> -d <span style="color:#e6db74">'{"message":"READY"}'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>check_listeners </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl -s -o /dev/null -w <span style="color:#e6db74">'%{http_code}\n'</span> http://127.0.0.1:18443/api/chat <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -H <span style="color:#e6db74">'Content-Type: application/json'</span> -d <span style="color:#e6db74">'{"message":"READY"}'</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 - <span style="color:#e6db74"><<'PY' | curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:18443/api/chat \ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74"> -H 'Authorization: Bearer FAKE_LOCAL_AI_LAB_TOKEN' \ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74"> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @- </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">import json </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">print(json.dumps({"message": "A" * 400})) </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span><span style="color:#e6db74">PY</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>kill <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$LAB_PID<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>wait <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$LAB_PID<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> 2>/dev/null <span style="color:#f92672">||</span> true </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>trap - EXIT </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Expected status codes are <code>200</code>, <code>401</code>, and <code>413</code> before restore, then <code>200</code>, <code>401</code>, and <code>200</code> after restore. Record both hashes, observed results, cleanup, and any test left <code>not run</code>. Do not expose the service during this drill. The synthetic lab does not prove a production runtime rollback.</p> <h2 id="acceptance-rubric"> <a href="#acceptance-rubric" title="Acceptance Rubric">Acceptance Rubric</a> <a href="#acceptance-rubric" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Acceptance Rubric">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Area</th> <th>Beginner pass</th> <th>Advanced pass</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Model</strong></td> <td>Source, license, identifier, and fit recorded</td> <td>Digest and artifact retention added</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Quality</strong></td> <td>Synthetic task reviewed</td> <td>Fixed evaluation set and acceptance rule</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Performance</strong></td> <td>Three warm single-user trials</td> <td>Context and concurrency measurements, plus observed timeout and overload results from the approved gateway. A test plan alone earns partial credit.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Network</strong></td> <td>Loopback-only runtime</td> <td>Private route through gateway to loopback runtime</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Identity</strong></td> <td>Host user boundary</td> <td>Per-user authentication and route authorization</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Logs</strong></td> <td>Local service and access record</td> <td>Central protected metadata with retention rule</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Prior configuration restored</td> <td>Runtime, model, driver, and policy rollback tested</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>Fail the review when the service exposes a native runtime port to an untrusted network, lacks a clear model license, stores unneeded full prompts, or has no tested rollback.</p> <h2 id="expected-result"> <a href="#expected-result" title="Expected Result">Expected Result</a> <a href="#expected-result" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Expected Result">#</a> </h2> <p>Your package ties every claim to a source or observed test. The deployment decision names scope, conditions, evidence gaps, residual risk, owner, and review date.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>The selected model changed during testing:</strong> Restart the benchmark record under one exact identifier.</li> <li><strong>Performance passes only after removing security controls:</strong> Measure the approved end-to-end path and revise capacity.</li> <li><strong>Gateway tests pass but runtime port is reachable remotely:</strong> Repair bind and firewall rules before approval.</li> <li><strong>Rollback restores service but access denial fails:</strong> Treat rollback as failed and repair the prior policy package.</li> <li><strong>The decision lacks a data class:</strong> Define allowed data before service approval.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verify-completion"> <a href="#verify-completion" title="Verify Completion">Verify Completion</a> <a href="#verify-completion" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Completion">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>find local-ai-capstone -maxdepth <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span> -type f -print | sort </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>grep -Ein <span style="color:#e6db74">"model|license|digest|loopback|authentication|rollback|owner"</span> <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> local-ai-capstone/deployment-decision.md </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Pass when all nine files exist and all track requirements have evidence. The beginner path must show a loopback-only listener and recorded firewall policy, with remote denial labeled <code>not run</code> if no second client exists. The advanced path must show an unauthorized gateway request denied in the synthetic lab plus observed timeout and concurrency overload results from the approved gateway. The synthetic lab does not test timeout or concurrency overload. The listener must match the design, rollback must pass the same checks, and the decision must name an owner for each remaining condition.</p> <p>After you finish the package and decision, compare them with the separate <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="capstone answer key"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course/09-capstone-answer-key/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course/09-capstone-answer-key/" rel="follow me" >capstone answer key</a> </span> .</p> <p>Return to the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="course hub"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/local-ai-secure-server-course-start/"> <a href="/local-ai-secure-server-course-start/" rel="follow me" >course hub</a> </span> . Review the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Ollama documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.ollama.com/"> <a href="https://docs.ollama.com/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Ollama documentation</a> </span> and <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="llama.cpp server documentation"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md"> <a href="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >llama.cpp server documentation</a> </span> before adapting commands to a newer release.</p> Read More at https://simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Capstone: Review a Secure Agent and MCP Design
item.description: Produce and evaluate a review-ready security package for an AI agent with MCP tools.
item.content:encoded: <p> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Return to the Secure AI Agents and MCP Course"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/secure-ai-agents-mcp-course-start/"> <a href="/secure-ai-agents-mcp-course-start/" rel="follow me" >Return to the Secure AI Agents and MCP Course</a> </span> </p> <p><strong>Your capstone is a security decision package for Patch Clerk.</strong> Another reviewer should reach the same deployment decision from your artifacts and evidence.</p> <h2 id="scenario-change"> <a href="#scenario-change" title="Scenario Change">Scenario Change</a> <a href="#scenario-change" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Scenario Change">#</a> </h2> <p>Patch Clerk now reads synthetic issues, reads repository files, proposes a patch, and applies a reviewed patch in a test repository. A product owner requests a new <code>post_comment</code> tool. The tool would publish text to a fictional issue system.</p> <p>Your job is to decide whether <code>post_comment</code> enters the first release. Treat publication as an external side effect.</p> <h2 id="required-package"> <a href="#required-package" title="Required Package">Required Package</a> <a href="#required-package" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Required Package">#</a> </h2> <p>Create <strong><code>capstone/</code></strong> with these files:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>capstone/ </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> system-map.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> authority-matrix.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> mcp-security-contract.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> event-example.json </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> detection-plan.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> attack-test.md </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> deployment-decision.md </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Each file has one purpose:</p> <ul> <li><strong><code>system-map.md</code></strong> names components, trust boundaries, data origins, and owners.</li> <li><strong><code>authority-matrix.md</code></strong> lists operations, identities, approval, and evidence.</li> <li><strong><code>mcp-security-contract.md</code></strong> defines inputs, outputs, limits, errors, and side effects.</li> <li><strong><code>event-example.json</code></strong> shows the decision event format without storing unnecessary raw content.</li> <li><strong><code>detection-plan.md</code></strong> maps signals to stop and recovery actions.</li> <li><strong><code>attack-test.md</code></strong> records the hostile fixture, expected result, observed result, and retest.</li> <li><strong><code>deployment-decision.md</code></strong> states approve, approve with conditions, or reject.</li> </ul> <h2 id="build-the-review"> <a href="#build-the-review" title="Build the Review">Build the Review</a> <a href="#build-the-review" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Build the Review">#</a> </h2> <ol> <li>Copy your lesson artifacts into <strong><code>capstone/</code></strong>.</li> <li>Add <code>post_comment</code> to the authority matrix as proposed.</li> <li>Define a 2,000-character limit and one approved issue target.</li> <li>Require a preview and trusted host-held, single-use approval bound to the comment digest and target-state precondition. A caller-supplied digest is not approval.</li> <li>Give the tool a dedicated identity restricted to comment creation on the approved test project.</li> <li>Add rate limits and a stop rule for repeated publication requests.</li> <li>Run the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="local comment policy simulator"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/downloads/secure-ai-agents-mcp-course/comment_policy_lab.py"> <a href="/downloads/secure-ai-agents-mcp-course/comment_policy_lab.py" rel="follow me" >local comment policy simulator</a> </span> with <code>python3 comment_policy_lab.py</code>. Record all nine expected and observed decisions in <strong><code>attack-test.md</code></strong>. Include the hostile denial, valid <code>would_post</code> decision, replay denial, forged self-approval denial, target and length denials, identity denial, changed-state denial, and rate-limit denial.</li> <li>Record your decision and residual risks.</li> </ol> <p>Do not connect a live issue service. Treat the capstone as a design and local policy test.</p> <h2 id="decision-rubric"> <a href="#decision-rubric" title="Decision Rubric">Decision Rubric</a> <a href="#decision-rubric" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Decision Rubric">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Area</th> <th>0 points</th> <th>1 point</th> <th>2 points</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Authority</strong></td> <td>Broad shared identity</td> <td>Narrow identity with gaps</td> <td>Dedicated least-privilege identity</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Input</strong></td> <td>Free-form unchecked payload</td> <td>Length or target check</td> <td>Typed input, target allowlist, and length limit</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Approval</strong></td> <td>None</td> <td>Approval before final payload</td> <td>Preview and digest-bound single-use approval</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Evidence</strong></td> <td>Model transcript only</td> <td>Host event</td> <td>Host, server, and downstream correlation</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Attack test</strong></td> <td>No hostile fixture</td> <td>Expected result only</td> <td>Observed local denial plus positive test</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Recovery</strong></td> <td>Restart only</td> <td>Revoke or restore</td> <td>Stop, revoke, preserve, restore, repair, retest</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>A score below <strong>10 out of 12</strong> fails the release review. Any zero in authority, approval, or attack test also fails.</p> <h2 id="expected-result"> <a href="#expected-result" title="Expected Result">Expected Result</a> <a href="#expected-result" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Expected Result">#</a> </h2> <p>Your package scores at least 10. It contains no real secrets or external connections. The decision states who owns remaining risk and which evidence is still missing for production.</p> <h2 id="troubleshooting"> <a href="#troubleshooting" title="Troubleshooting">Troubleshooting</a> <a href="#troubleshooting" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Troubleshooting">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>The package repeats chat transcripts:</strong> Replace narrative with maps, contracts, events, diffs, and test results.</li> <li><strong>The comment identity reaches every project:</strong> Restrict the downstream account before relying on server input checks.</li> <li><strong>Approval lacks a payload digest:</strong> Bind approval to the final issue target and comment text.</li> <li><strong>The attack test blocks valid comments:</strong> Add a positive test and repair the narrow policy path.</li> <li><strong>Residual risk has no owner:</strong> Assign a named role with a review date and acceptance decision.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verify-completion"> <a href="#verify-completion" title="Verify Completion">Verify Completion</a> <a href="#verify-completion" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Verify Completion">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>find capstone -maxdepth <span style="color:#ae81ff">1</span> -type f -print | sort </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>python3 -m json.tool capstone/event-example.json </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>grep -Ein <span style="color:#e6db74">"decision|owner|residual|approval|digest"</span> capstone/deployment-decision.md </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Pass when all seven files exist, JSON parses, the rubric score reaches ten, no core area scores zero, and the decision separates observed local evidence from future production tests.
